title: Add Ultimate Multisite troubleshooting skill and diagnostic routing
body:
## Scope correction

This issue should not make SuperDav AI Agent reimplement Ultimate Multisite domain, tenant, hosting, or limitation diagnostics. Ultimate Multisite should own those authoritative facts and expose them through an ability/API. SuperDav should add the skill and routing needed to use that capability correctly during outage/support conversations.

Authoritative Ultimate Multisite diagnostic task: Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite#1629

## Problem

During a production outage, a mapped Ultimate Multisite customer site looked offline from the public web: `/` returned HTTP 404 with WordPress title `Not available` and body `This site is not available at this time.` DNS, TLS, REST, and login were healthy. The real cause was an Ultimate Multisite visit-limit lock on the mapped tenant.

SuperDav AI Agent had generic WordPress troubleshooting skills, but it did not know the Ultimate Multisite diagnostic sequence:

1. Start with a public availability check, not only WP admin/site-health internals.
2. Verify the live document root / WordPress context; do not assume a similarly named directory is the served install.
3. Resolve mapped domain -> tenant blog/site using Ultimate Multisite capabilities.
4. Ask Ultimate Multisite for tenant/domain/limit lock reasons rather than guessing from generic WordPress options.

## Proposed implementation

Add an `ultimate-multisite` skill (or expand the existing `multisite-management` skill with an Ultimate Multisite-specific section) that is auto-loaded when the repo/plugin exposes Ultimate Multisite abilities or when the user mentions mapped domains, tenant sites, WaaS, WP Ultimo, Ultimate Multisite, custom domain mapping, visit limits, or `Not available` frontend locks.

The skill should teach this diagnostic workflow:

### 1. Public smoke check first

Use available HTTP/browser/site tools to inspect the public URL before internal WordPress checks:

- DNS/host resolution if available
- TLS/transport if available
- redirect chain / effective URL
- HTTP status
- page title
- short body fingerprint
- detection for WordPress `wp_die` pages such as title `Not available` and body `This site is not available at this time.`

If SuperDav lacks low-level DNS/TLS tools in a given runtime, state that and perform the HTTP status/body fingerprint check it can do.

### 2. Verify live WordPress targeting

Use WordPress context abilities/WP-CLI to verify the actual site context:

- `home_url()` / `site_url()`
- `is_multisite()`
- `get_current_blog_id()`
- `ABSPATH` or safe install identifier
- If using WP-CLI, always include `--url=<public URL>` for mapped multisite domains

### 3. Delegate Ultimate Multisite facts to Ultimate Multisite

When Ultimate Multisite abilities are present, prefer them over generic `db-query` or `run-php`:

- Search/select `multisite-ultimate/*` abilities for site/domain/customer/membership lookups
- Once Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite#1629 exists, call `multisite-ultimate/site-availability-diagnose` (or the final chosen name)
- Use its response for domain mapping state, tenant type, customer/membership IDs, limitations, monthly visits, and lock reason

Only use `db-query` as a fallback if no Ultimate Multisite ability exists, and then keep it read-only and narrowly scoped.

### 4. Report safely

The agent should report:

- whether the public frontend is actually unavailable
- whether REST/login/admin are healthy
- which live WordPress install/site context was targeted
- the Ultimate Multisite lock reason if available
- recommended next action requiring approval for writes, e.g. raise/disable visit limit, fix domain mapping stage, unarchive site

It must not update limitations, flush caches, activate plugins, or change options unless the user explicitly approves remediation.

## Likely files

- `includes/Models/skills/multisite-management.md`
- new `includes/Models/skills/ultimate-multisite.md` if a separate skill is clearer
- `includes/Models/skills/site-troubleshooting.md`
- `includes/Infrastructure/WordPress/Abilities/UsageInstructionsFilter.php`
- any skill auto-load/matching tests

## Acceptance criteria

- SuperDav has an Ultimate Multisite troubleshooting skill or equivalent skill section that documents the public-smoke -> live-context -> mapped-domain -> Ultimate Multisite diagnostic sequence.
- The skill explicitly says to use Ultimate Multisite abilities for tenant/domain/limit state, especially the diagnostic ability from Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite#1629 once available.
- The generic troubleshooting skill tells the agent to run a public URL check first and to verify live document root/context before assuming a local directory is the served install.
- The multisite skill tells the agent to use `--url=<public mapped domain>` for WP-CLI/context checks on mapped domains.

## Summary

PR #2224 merged SuperDav-side availability diagnostics for mapped Ultimate Multisite tenant locks. That no longer matches the corrected ownership boundary.

New direction:

- Ultimate Multisite owns authoritative tenant/domain/hosting/limit/lock diagnostics. See Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite#1629 and PR Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite#1630.
- SuperDav AI Agent should not duplicate Ultimate Multisite SQL, visit-limit calculations, domain mapping lookups, or lock-reason logic.
- SuperDav should only provide skill/prompt routing that tells the agent when and how to call Ultimate Multisite abilities/API, plus generic public smoke guidance if that remains useful outside Ultimate Multisite.

## What to change

Review merged PR #2224 and undo/refactor it as needed.

PR #2224 changed:

- `includes/Abilities/SiteHealthAbilities.php`
- `includes/Models/skills/multisite-management.md`
- `includes/Models/skills/site-troubleshooting.md`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/SiteHealthAbilitiesTest.php`

Required cleanup:

1. Remove or revert Ultimate Multisite-specific tenant/visit-limit lock detection from `SiteHealthAbilities`.
   - No direct `wu_*` meta inspection in SuperDav.
   - No SuperDav-owned monthly visit total calculations.
   - No SuperDav-owned Ultimate Multisite lock reason inference.
   - No fallback that encourages `db-query`/raw SQL as the normal path when an Ultimate Multisite ability should exist.

2. Replace that with delegation guidance.
   - If Ultimate Multisite abilities are present, SuperDav should discover/call the relevant `multisite-ultimate/*` ability.
   - Once Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite#1629 lands, the expected call should be the final `site-availability-diagnose` ability/API name from that work.
   - Until then, the skill may state that authoritative tenant lock diagnostics are unavailable and recommend using Ultimate Multisite admin/API, not guessing.

3. Keep or rewrite only the useful generic parts.
   - It is okay to keep generic public frontend smoke guidance in `site-troubleshooting.md`: check public URL first, HTTP status/title/body fingerprint, compare REST/login/admin health.
   - If `site-health-summary` keeps any public smoke check, keep it generic WordPress availability only. Do not include Ultimate Multisite-specific tenant/domain/limit logic there.

4. Add or update the Ultimate Multisite skill path.
   - Prefer a dedicated `includes/Models/skills/ultimate-multisite.md` or a clearly separated Ultimate Multisite section in `multisite-management.md`.
   - It should say: public smoke first -> verify live WordPress context (`ABSPATH`, `home_url()`, `get_current_blog_id()`, `--url=<mapped-domain>`) -> call Ultimate Multisite abilities for domain/tenant/lock facts.

5. Update tests.

   - Add/keep tests that assert the skill/guidance routes Ultimate Multisite lock diagnosis to Ultimate Multisite abilities.

- SuperDav no longer contains duplicated Ultimate Multisite tenant/domain/visit-limit lock logic introduced by PR #2224.
- SuperDav skill/prompt guidance clearly delegates authoritative Ultimate Multisite diagnostics to Ultimate Multisite #1629/#1630.

This should remain blocked/no-auto-dispatch until the Ultimate Multisite diagnostic ability/API in Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite#1629/#1630 is merged or its final shape is known. title: Prevent provider payload-limit failures before request dispatch
body:
## What

Prevent upstream HTTP 413 failures before the configured AI provider or proxy receives an oversized chat request. Preserve a safe, usable continuation instead of only surfacing an error.

## Why

The chat path delegates requests through the WordPress AI Client SDK, so `Client error (413)` identifies a rejection by the selected provider or intermediary, not OpenAI specifically. The current plugin cannot measure or attribute the rejected request safely enough to decide whether the provider should accept a larger body.

Existing compaction is insufficient:

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` applies `ConversationTrimmer::trim()` only after the history exceeds the turn count in `max_history_turns` (default 20).
- `includes/Core/ConversationTrimmer.php` preserves the entire first turn and has no byte or token budget, so one oversized early turn can remain indefinitely.
- `src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js` builds `/compact` by sending the entire transcript as a new summary prompt, which can itself exceed the same request limit.

## Worker Guidance

### Files to Modify

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — identify provider 413s, invoke a single safe fallback only when it reduces the outgoing request, and retain recoverable session state.
- `includes/Core/ConversationTrimmer.php` — add a byte/token-budget compaction path that preserves valid tool-call/result pairs without permanently retaining an oversized first turn.
- `src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js` — replace client-side full-transcript `/compact` submission with a bounded, server-backed summary flow or deterministic chunked compaction.
- `includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php` — record provider ID, model ID, status, and request-size metadata only; do not log prompts, attachments, credentials, or raw request bodies.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AgentLoopTest.php`, `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/ConversationTrimmerTest.php`, and the relevant JS store test — cover the fallback, budget reduction, tool-pair validity, and bounded compaction request.

### Implementation Constraints

- Do not assume the rejection came from OpenAI. Use the runtime-selected provider/model and safe request-size telemetry to establish attribution.
- Do not retry an unchanged 413 request. Limit any automatic fallback to one attempt and only after demonstrably reducing the request.
- Keep provider credentials, prompt text, attachment bytes, and raw request bodies out of traces, REST responses, and logs.
- Preserve the existing `max_history_turns` behaviour as a secondary guard; the new budget must cover payload bytes/tokens, not only message count.
- Keep tool-use/tool-result cycles valid after each trim.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A request over the configured safety budget is compacted or rejected locally with actionable guidance before an identical oversized request is sent upstream.
2. A provider 413 records only safe diagnostics sufficient to identify the selected provider/model and request-size class.
3. `/compact` never submits the whole unbounded transcript as its summary prompt.

## What

Define and enforce one semantic palette-role contract for generated block themes:

- Required: `foreground`, `background`, `surface`, `accent`, `on-accent`

- body and headings: `foreground` on `background`

A palette generated exactly from current guidance can therefore report a pass without checking its body or heading contrast.

- **Conversation context:** Design-system research found that two shipped ability groups independently locate, create, merge, and delete `wp_global_styles` records using different identity rules.

## What

Introduce one `GlobalStylesService` that owns active-theme user Global Styles persistence and resolved-style reads. Route these existing public abilities through it without changing their IDs, schemas, capability gates, multisite behavior, or response contracts:

- `sd-ai-agent/get-global-styles`
- `sd-ai-agent/update-global-styles`
- `sd-ai-agent/reset-global-styles`
- `sd-ai-agent/theme-json-presets`

The service must distinguish:

1. WordPress's resolved active-theme style view.
2. The complete user-level `wp_global_styles` document.
3. Partial `settings`/`styles` merges into that document.
4. Canonical lookup/create/delete for only the active stylesheet's customization.

## Why

- `GlobalStylesAbilities` identifies posts through active-theme metadata and creates a canonical post at `includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php:514-599`.
- `DesignSystemAbilities` searches by `post_name`, then can fall back to any recently published Global Styles post at `includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php:761-792`.
- Its update path can create a post without the same canonical identity metadata at `includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php:661-704`.
- Both classes independently decode, merge, encode, update, and delete the same persisted document.

One ability can therefore update a record another cannot find, or select a record belonging to another theme. This must be corrected before generated design tokens and style variations rely on Global Styles.

## Tier

**Selected:** `tier:thinking`

Six coordinated files, two classes over 500 lines, persistent-data compatibility, multisite restoration, and competing lookup rules disqualify `tier:simple` and `tier:standard`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- Stop when the resolved read, canonical active-theme record, create/update/delete identity, and multisite boundaries are explicit.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php:268-375,433-467,507-648` — delegate while preserving public behavior

- **Callers/readers:** `GlobalStylesAbilities.php:268-294`; `DesignSystemAbilities.php:420-435,628-653`
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `GlobalStylesAbilities.php:302-375,433-467`; `DesignSystemAbilities.php:661-750`

### Implementation Steps

1. Characterize current WordPress 7.0 resolver/create behavior with failing service tests, including competing theme records.
2. Implement typed methods for `get_resolved_styles()`, `get_user_document()`, `merge_user_document()`, and `delete_user_document()`.
3. Base canonical identity on the active stylesheet; remove the unrestricted latest-post fallback.
4. Move JSON handling, deep merge, canonical create/update, and delete into the service.
5. Keep multisite switching and frontend `affected` descriptors in the ability façade, restoring the original blog on every exit path.
6. Delegate `theme-json-presets` persistence to the same service while preserving its action/result contract.
7. Add cross-façade tests proving both APIs observe and mutate one active-theme document.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** repeated concurrent merges must not create duplicate posts; prefer WordPress's canonical resolver where possible.
- **Migration/rollback:** historical noncanonical posts may exist; never select or delete an arbitrary record, and preserve prior content on rollback.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** preserve every shipped ability ID, schema, response key, capability, and error code.
- **Idempotency/retry:** identical merges reuse one post; repeated reset with no customization remains successful.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** encoding or update failure leaves the previous document intact and returns `WP_Error`.
- **Isolation:** stylesheet A's record must never be touched while stylesheet B is active.

title: Add maturity and version governance for generated design artifacts
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `design artifact maturity governance` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery: 0 overlapping open PRs and no direct duplicate issue
- [x] File refs verified at `c67f71b75152eb4ff4cdd3bf746777d7bcb45112`

- [x] Seeded PR: skipped — issue-only planning task

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-18
- **Created by:** AI DevOps, interactive research session
- **Blocked by:** #2247 (`blocked-by:#2247`)
- **Conversation context:** Generated token sets, block patterns, and style variations need shared maturity, provenance, compatibility, selection, and rollback semantics before their dedicated producers are implemented.

## What

Introduce a canonical manifest, selector, and release contract for generated design artifacts:

- `token_set`
- `pattern`
- `style_variation`

Every artifact record must include:

- stable namespaced `id` and semantic `version`
- `maturity`: `stable`, `candidate`, `experimental`, or `deprecated`
- provenance: generator/plugin version, source type/reference, timestamp, input hash
- compatibility: WordPress range, theme.json version, required blocks/features, theme constraints
- deprecation reason, replacement, and removal target when applicable
- canonical integrity/content hash

Selection policy:

1. Reject incompatible artifacts first.
2. Honor an exact compatible site/user pin.
3. Otherwise choose the highest compatible `stable` version.
4. Require explicit opt-in for `candidate` and per-artifact opt-in for `experimental`.
5. Never select `deprecated` for a new build or cross a semantic-major version automatically.
6. Preserve an already-selected deprecated artifact until replacement/rollback is explicitly chosen.
7. Resolve ties deterministically; filesystem/database order must not matter.

Release policy:

- Stage and validate every output before changing the active manifest pointer.
- Snapshot the prior files and affected WordPress records needed for exact rollback.
- On failure, restore the previous complete release rather than leaving mixed artifacts.
- Roll back by exact release ID after verifying retained hashes.

## Why

Current operations have no shared lifecycle metadata:

- curated patterns: `includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php:84-147,446-620`
- theme presets/Global Styles: `includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php:200-245,628-750`
- block-theme guidance: `includes/Models/skills/wp-block-themes.md:173-268`
- generated theme baseline: `advanced-plugin/includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php:190-275,460-491`

Without governance, generator upgrades can silently change output, experimental assets can become defaults, compatibility decisions cannot be explained, and rollback cannot reproduce the prior design.

## Tier

**Selected:** `tier:thinking`

The schema and resolver become a long-lived contract across core abilities, advanced scaffolding, filesystem artifacts, `wp_block`, and `wp_global_styles`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- Read `includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php:84-147,200-245,446-750` first.
- Read `advanced-plugin/includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php:190-275,460-491` and `includes/Models/skills/wp-block-themes.md:173-268` next.
- Inspect existing revision/GitTracker services only if they can provide complete multi-artifact snapshots.
- Stop when all current/future writes map to one manifest/release transaction.
- `DESIGN.md` was checked; no plugin UI is required, so leave it unchanged unless a management screen is added.

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: includes/DesignSystem/ArtifactManifest.php`
- `NEW: includes/DesignSystem/ArtifactSelector.php`
- `NEW: includes/DesignSystem/ArtifactReleaseManager.php`
- `NEW: includes/DesignSystem/design-artifact-manifest.schema.json`
- `NEW: includes/Abilities/DesignSystemArtifactAbilities.php`
- `EDIT: includes/Bootstrap/AbilitiesHandler.php`
- `EDIT: includes/Abilities/ToolCapabilities.php:122-136`
- `EDIT: includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php:84-147,200-245`
- `EDIT: advanced-plugin/includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php:190-275`
- `EDIT: includes/Models/skills/wp-block-themes.md:173-268`
- `NEW: tests/SdAiAgent/DesignSystem/ArtifactManifestTest.php`
- `NEW: tests/SdAiAgent/DesignSystem/ArtifactSelectorTest.php`
- `NEW: tests/SdAiAgent/DesignSystem/ArtifactReleaseManagerTest.php`
- `NEW: tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/DesignSystemArtifactAbilitiesTest.php`
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbilityTest.php:393-474`
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Models/BlockThemesSkillTest.php:46-98`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `DesignSystemArtifactAbilities.php`, generated-theme orchestration, and downstream producers
- **Writers/mutation paths:** generated `theme.json`, `patterns/*.php`, `styles/*.json`, governed `wp_block`/`wp_global_styles`, snapshots, and active manifest pointer
- **Tests/fixtures:** `tests/SdAiAgent/DesignSystem/` covers manifests, selection, release, maturity, hashes, and failures
- **Schemas/config:** `design-artifact-manifest.schema.json` plus `ArtifactManifest.php` parser/normalizer
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** immutable source/snapshots stay outside WordPress auto-discovery; only selected files materialize into `patterns/`/`styles/`
- **Migrations/backfills:** do not silently import third-party artifacts; explicit known-generated legacy import is `experimental` `0.0.0` with `legacy-untracked` provenance
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `ArtifactReleaseManager.php` retains active/previous/pinned/replacement releases and exact hashes

### Implementation Steps

1. Implement strict schema-v1 parsing, canonical serialization, and hashing. Reject invalid SemVer, maturity, provenance, compatibility, deprecation, and integrity records.
2. Implement pure deterministic selection with an ordered decision trace for every accepted/rejected candidate.
3. Implement release transactions: snapshot → stage → validate → materialize → update active pointer last; compensate completed writes in reverse order on failure.
4. Keep inactive immutable source payloads outside WordPress auto-discovery paths.
5. Add separate list/inspect/resolve/apply/rollback abilities with accurate capability and destructive annotations.
6. Route only declared generated-artifact writes through the release manager; preserve ordinary user-created patterns and customizations.
7. Seed generated themes with a valid empty/current manifest without adding opinionated design defaults.
8. Document the API for token, pattern, and style-variation producer issues; they must not define parallel maturity metadata.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** serialize release activation per site/theme; update the active pointer last.
- **Migration/rollback:** never mutate third-party themes during import; snapshot before any materialization and restore exact prior release.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** unknown manifest versions fail upgrade-required; readers may accept additive fields but reject unknown required semantics.
- **Idempotency/retry:** applying an identical release/hash is a no-op; retry after compensation starts from restored state.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** filesystem and WordPress-record writes are compensated in reverse order and tested with injected failures.
- **SemVer:** use numeric SemVer including prerelease precedence, never lexical ordering.
- **Security:** sanitize IDs/paths, prevent traversal, and never execute artifact source to inspect metadata.
- **User ownership:** never silently import, deprecate, rewrite, or delete third-party themes or ordinary user patterns.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='ArtifactManifestTest|ArtifactSelectorTest|ArtifactReleaseManagerTest|DesignSystemArtifactAbilitiesTest|ScaffoldBlockThemeAbilityTest|BlockThemesSkillTest'
rg -n "stable|candidate|experimental|deprecated|provenance|compatibility|rollback" includes/DesignSystem includes/Models/skills/wp-block-themes.md
npm run verify
```

- **Surface mapping:** manifest tests prove schema/integrity, selector tests prove policy, release tests prove compensation/rollback, scaffold tests preserve minimal defaults, and full verification covers packaging/shared APIs.

Create a WIP commit after focused tests and before the full gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Schema v1 validates all three artifact kinds with stable IDs, SemVer, maturity, provenance, compatibility, deprecation, and integrity.
- [ ] Selection follows the specified compatibility, pin, maturity, SemVer, and tie-break rules with a deterministic decision trace.
- [ ] Automatic selection never chooses deprecated artifacts for new builds or crosses semantic-major versions.
- [ ] A release is fully staged and validated before the active pointer changes.
- [ ] Injected failure after any file, `wp_block`, or `wp_global_styles` write restores the previous complete release.
- [ ] Exact rollback still works after newer registry entries are added.
- [ ] Third-party themes and ordinary user patterns are not silently imported or rewritten.
- [ ] New generated themes contain a valid initial manifest while preserving the minimal scaffold baseline.
- [ ] Downstream token, pattern, and style-variation issues can consume one documented API without parallel metadata.
- [ ] Focused tests and `npm run verify` pass with zero errors and failures.

## What

Introduce a versioned design-token contract, strict validator/normalizer, and pure compiler that emits:

- complete WordPress `theme.json` with the canonical schema and `version: 3`
- compatible user Global Styles `settings` and `styles` payloads
- native presets for colors, font families, font sizes, and spacing
- custom values for unsupported primitives such as radii/shadows where appropriate
- stable semantic roles such as `background`, `foreground`, `surface`, `primary`, `on-primary`, `accent`, `on-accent`, `border`, body/heading typography, content/section spacing, and control radius

- governance metadata required by #2248

Expose a read-only `sd-ai-agent/compile-design-tokens` ability. It must not write files, options, posts, or Global Styles; callers explicitly pass compiled outputs to existing mutation abilities.

Required hierarchy:

```text
reference primitives → semantic roles → element/block aliases → WordPress presets and styles
```

- `theme-json-presets` accepts arbitrary partial data at `includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php:200-245`.
- `update-global-styles` accepts raw `settings` and `styles` at `includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php:75-176`.

- Setup Assistant independently reconstructs theme and Global Styles data at `includes/Models/Agent.php:676-707`.
- `includes/Models/skills/wp-block-themes.md:173-233` documents presets but has no machine-validated design contract.

These independent payloads can drift. Stable semantic aliases also make style variations possible without rewriting page markup.

## Tier

**Selected:** `tier:thinking`

There is no existing contract to copy. The worker must design a safe schema that maps to WordPress 7.0 theme.json v3, the canonical persistence service from #2247, palette roles from #2246, and governance from #2248.

## Tier

**Selected:** `tier:thinking`

## How (Approach)

## Pre-flight

- `list-style-variations`

- `update-style-variation`
- `validate-style-variation`
- `preview-style-variation`
- `select-style-variation`

- list child/parent variations with slug/title/origin/relative path/read-only/hash/selection state

- update complete documents with required `expected_hash`; inherited parent files are read-only

- select by applying a validated variation to user Global Styles while storing an exact plugin-owned baseline and resulting hash

Use separate ability contracts, not a generic action dispatcher.

## Why

The skill documents `styles/*.json` at `wp-block-themes.md:14-19,42-49`, but no dedicated lifecycle exists. Generic file mutation does not understand validation, inheritance, previews, or concurrency. `reset-global-styles` deletes the entire customization post at `GlobalStylesAbilities.php:428-467`, which is unsafe for variation rollback.

## Tier

**Selected:** `tier:thinking`

Seven contracts cross advanced filesystem writes, core capability mapping, WordPress theme JSON resolution, Global Styles selection state, preview compilation, and rollback.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Writers/mutation paths:** create/update active stylesheet files; select/reset active-theme Global Styles plus a site-scoped `sd_ai_agent_` provenance option

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-18
- **Created by:** AI DevOps, interactive research session
- **Blocked by:** #2250, #2251, #2252 (`blocked-by:#2250`, `blocked-by:#2251`, `blocked-by:#2252`)
- **Conversation context:** Existing guidance asks for final review but allows structural fallback. Generated themes can still be declared complete without rendering and validating the actual activated WordPress frontend.

## What

Add a hard generated-theme completion gate. After activation, render the actual homepage and one representative interior page—not standalone design-direction HTML—at:

| Viewport | Size |
|---|---|
| Mobile | 375×812 |
| Tablet | 768×1024 |
| Desktop | 1280×800 |

Run deterministic responsive, accessibility, content, activation, and render-health checks. The report must be tied to the expected active stylesheet and current generated-theme fingerprint. Setup Assistant cannot report completion until the current report passes.

Minimum checks:

- expected stylesheet is active and required URLs render successfully
- no document-level horizontal overflow
- visible header/navigation/main/footer and one page-level heading
- valid heading order, language, landmarks, duplicate IDs
- images have valid alternative-text treatment
- links/controls have accessible names and visible usable focus
- governed foreground/background pairs meet agreed WCAG thresholds
- no placeholders, empty/hash-only CTA, unprovided remote stock image, broken local asset, or hidden essential content
- reduced-motion mode does not leave content hidden
- each violation names URL, viewport, selector/evidence, severity, and remediation

Browser unavailability or partial execution is incomplete, never a pass.

## Why

- Final review remains advisory at `includes/Models/skills/wp-block-themes.md:42-51,525-535`.
- Setup Assistant activates then proceeds toward success at `includes/Models/Agent.php:676-695`.
- `RenderDesignPreviewsAbility.php:47-173` and `PreviewRenderer.php:54-123` render standalone direction artifacts, not the activated theme.
- Existing preview E2E at `tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js:616-819` is based on standalone HTML.

This issue turns quality evidence into an enforceable invariant and prevents stale preview screenshots or subjective approval from satisfying completion.

## Tier

**Selected:** `tier:thinking`

The change spans AgentLoop final-response handling, PHP gate state, browser abilities, build output, prompts/skills, and E2E failure/recovery.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- Load only the AgentLoop final-response/tool-result path needed to enforce the invariant.

- **Writers/mutation paths:** `GeneratedThemeCompletionGate.php` writes per-job state; theme/page/Global Styles writers invalidate it

- [ ] Standalone preview HTML, cached PNGs, subjective approval, and structural-only review cannot satisfy the gate.
- [ ] Reports contain deterministic responsive/accessibility/content/render/activation evidence with remediation.
- [ ] Any relevant mutation invalidates the report and requires a rerun.
- [ ] Browser unavailability, timeout, missing interior content, or partial execution never passes.
- [ ] Fatal/unrenderable activation restores the previous stylesheet; repairable quality failures remain incomplete and repairable.
- [ ] E2E injects at least one overflow or accessibility violation and proves completion is withheld until fixed.
- [ ] Focused JS/PHP tests, E2E, and `npm run verify` pass.

- **Blocked by:** #2250, #2251, #2252
- **Blocks:** reliable automated claims that a generated theme is complete

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-18
- **Created by:** AI DevOps, interactive post-merge review
- **Source:** merged PR #2256 / completed issue #2246
- **Blocked by:** none
- **Conversation context:** Review found that an explicitly empty or fully malformed custom pair override can bypass every contrast check, while the Setup Assistant immediately scaffolds after validation without requiring a passing result.

## What

Make palette validation fail closed when a supplied custom pair override contains no usable pairs, and make the Setup Assistant revalidate corrections and require `passed === true` before scaffolding a block theme.

Preserve valid custom-pair behavior and all existing canonical semantic role names.

## Why

- `includes/Abilities/ValidatePaletteContrastAbility.php:68-82` allows `pairs: []` because the schema has no non-empty constraint.
- `includes/Abilities/ValidatePaletteContrastAbility.php:154-157` forwards that empty array as a real override.
- `includes/Services/PaletteValidator.php:314-371` normalizes empty or fully malformed overrides to zero pairs.
- `includes/Services/PaletteValidator.php:247-254` then reports `passed: true` when a complete role palette has no failures or missing roles, even though `pairs_checked` and `pairs_expected` are both zero.
- `includes/Models/Agent.php:682-683` tells the Setup Assistant to auto-apply suggestions and then immediately scaffold; it does not require a second validation result with `passed === true`.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Services/PaletteValidatorTest.php:374-393` covers dropping one malformed entry only when another valid pair survives, so it does not protect against the zero-pair false pass.

This permits generated themes to claim WCAG validation without evaluating a single contrast pair.

## Tier

**Selected:** `tier:standard`

The implementation is bounded, but it coordinates the service, public ability schema/callback, agent prompt, and three focused test surfaces.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/Abilities/ValidatePaletteContrastAbility.php:51-85,145-157`
- `EDIT: includes/Services/PaletteValidator.php:198-254,314-371`
- `EDIT: includes/Models/Agent.php:676-685`
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/ValidatePaletteContrastAbilityTest.php`
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Services/PaletteValidatorTest.php:374-393`
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Models/AgentThemeBuilderTest.php`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** Setup Assistant prompt at `includes/Models/Agent.php:676-695`; ability registration remains unchanged.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** palette validation is read-only; `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme` is the downstream mutation that must remain gated by a passing result.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/ValidatePaletteContrastAbilityTest.php`, `tests/SdAiAgent/Services/PaletteValidatorTest.php`, and `tests/SdAiAgent/Models/AgentThemeBuilderTest.php` must encode the fail-closed sequence.
- **Schemas/config:** add a non-empty constraint to the optional `pairs` ability input while retaining the existing pair item schema.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** no generated source mirror; the built-in Setup Assistant prompt is generated directly from `Agent.php`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because palette validation and the built-in prompt persist no data.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because reverting the edits to `ValidatePaletteContrastAbility.php`, `PaletteValidator.php`, and `Agent.php` restores the previous behavior without data cleanup.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add a schema-level non-empty constraint for a supplied `pairs` override.
2. Add callback-level defense so an explicitly empty array, or an override whose entries all normalize away, cannot return a successful ability result.
3. Ensure direct `PaletteValidator` use can never report `passed: true` when `pairs_expected === 0`.
4. Preserve the default pair set when `pairs` is omitted and preserve valid custom overrides when at least one valid pair remains.
5. Update the Setup Assistant prompt to inspect the result, repair missing roles/failures, re-run `validate-palette-contrast`, and call `scaffold-block-theme` only after a result whose `passed` field is exactly true.
6. Add regression tests for `pairs: []`, an all-malformed override, mixed malformed/valid entries, and prompt ordering/pass gating.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** validation is in-memory and read-only.
- **Migration/rollback:** no stored state or migration.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** omission of `pairs` still uses defaults; non-empty valid custom overrides remain supported.
- **Idempotency/retry:** identical input returns the same result or stable validation error.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** the agent must repair and revalidate rather than scaffold after a failed or unevaluated result.
- Do not alias, rename, or migrate canonical palette slugs.
- Do not treat zero checks as a pass, even when all required palette roles are present.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='PaletteValidatorTest|ValidatePaletteContrastAbilityTest|AgentThemeBuilderTest'
rg -n "minItems|pairs_expected|passed|validate-palette-contrast|scaffold-block-theme" includes/Abilities/ValidatePaletteContrastAbility.php includes/Services/PaletteValidator.php includes/Models/Agent.php tests/SdAiAgent/
npm run verify
```

- **Surface mapping:** focused tests cover schema/callback validation, direct service behavior, valid custom overrides, and the built-in agent sequence; `npm run verify` covers regressions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pairs: []` cannot produce a successful `passed: true` result.
- [ ] An override whose entries all normalize away cannot produce a successful `passed: true` result.
- [ ] Direct service use reports `passed: false` whenever zero pairs are expected/evaluated.
- [ ] Omitting `pairs` still evaluates the default body, heading, link, and control pairs.
- [ ] A non-empty valid custom override retains its current behavior.
- [ ] The Setup Assistant repairs failures or missing roles, revalidates, and scaffolds only after `passed === true`.
- [ ] Existing semantic role names and ability IDs remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused tests and `npm run verify` pass with zero errors and failures.

title: Make Global Styles adoption failures atomic
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `design-system GlobalStylesService review` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery: no overlapping open issue or PR for resolver error propagation or failed legacy-adoption rollback
- [x] File refs verified at `f791c2f61ded202bbdc8f782da03a5dd17dea249`
- [x] WordPress source verified: `WP_Theme_JSON_Resolver::get_user_data_from_wp_global_styles()` calls `wp_insert_post(..., true)` but discards its `WP_Error` and returns an empty array
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — persisted data, rollback, canonical identity, and public error compatibility require architectural judgment
- [x] Seeded PR: skipped — post-merge review follow-up

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-18
- **Created by:** AI DevOps, interactive post-merge review
- **Source:** merged PR #2257 / completed issue #2247
- **Blocked by:** none
- **Conversation context:** Review found two failure paths that violate the original persistence guarantees: canonical-create errors are collapsed, and failed legacy adoption can leave partial mutation before a second canonical record is created.

## What

Harden `GlobalStylesService` failure handling so that:

1. Canonical active-theme post creation preserves actionable `WP_Error` details instead of collapsing every resolver failure into `global_styles_create_failed`.
2. Legacy-post adoption is atomic from the caller's perspective: content and `wp_theme` assignment are either both committed or both restored, and a failed adoption cannot fall through to creation of a duplicate canonical record.

Keep every public ability ID, response shape, capability gate, and façade-level error contract unchanged.

## Why

- `includes/Services/GlobalStylesService.php:208-217` calls the resolver's create path and returns a generic `global_styles_create_failed` whenever no post is returned.
- WordPress 7.0's `WP_Theme_JSON_Resolver::get_user_data_from_wp_global_styles()` calls `wp_insert_post(..., true)` internally but discards the returned `WP_Error`; the current service therefore loses the underlying failure code/message.
- The completed #2247 acceptance criteria explicitly required preservation of existing error codes and partial failures leaving prior content intact.
- `includes/Services/GlobalStylesService.php:303-326` rewrites a legacy post's JSON before assigning the active `wp_theme` term.
- If `ensure_active_theme_assignment()` fails at `includes/Services/GlobalStylesService.php:328-330`, the method returns `null` but leaves the rewritten content behind.
- The caller then treats adoption as absent and can create a new canonical post, leaving a mutated legacy record plus a duplicate active-theme document.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Services/GlobalStylesServiceTest.php:103-136` covers only successful adoption; there is no injected create, term-assignment, update, or rollback failure coverage.

## Tier

**Selected:** `tier:thinking`

The changes are localized to one service and tests, but require explicit transaction-like rollback around two WordPress APIs and careful compatibility across both public façades.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- Read `includes/Services/GlobalStylesService.php:83-175,177-403` first.
- Compare pre-#2257 error behavior in `includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php` and `includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php` only as needed.
- Inspect WordPress 7.0 `WP_Theme_JSON_Resolver::get_user_data_from_wp_global_styles()` and `wp_insert_post()` failure behavior before selecting the canonical creation path.
- Stop when exact create errors, original content/terms, rollback order, and duplicate-prevention behavior are covered by tests.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/Services/GlobalStylesService.php:83-149,177-403`
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Services/GlobalStylesServiceTest.php:103-241`
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilitiesTest.php` only if façade error compatibility needs explicit coverage
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilitiesTest.php` only if façade error compatibility needs explicit coverage

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `GlobalStylesAbilities` and `DesignSystemAbilities` both consume `merge_user_document()`, `delete_user_document()`, and user/resolved reads.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** canonical create/update/delete at `GlobalStylesService.php:89-174,208-229`; legacy content and taxonomy adoption at `GlobalStylesService.php:241-335`.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `tests/SdAiAgent/Services/GlobalStylesServiceTest.php`, `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilitiesTest.php`, and `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilitiesTest.php` cover service failures and externally visible behavior.
- **Schemas/config:** `includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php` and `includes/Abilities/DesignSystemAbilities.php` retain their existing IDs, schemas, capabilities, and REST visibility.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** N/A because the service is loaded directly through the existing Composer PSR-4 mapping and has no generated source mirror.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because this remains bounded on-access adoption of one unambiguous record; no bulk persisted-data migration is permitted.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `includes/Services/GlobalStylesService.php` must delete a newly created post after update failure, restore original legacy content and terms after adoption failure, and clean caches only after a committed change.

### Implementation Steps

1. Characterize and test the exact error returned when canonical post insertion fails.
2. Use a creation path that retains the underlying `WP_Error` while preserving WordPress's canonical post name, status, content, and `wp_theme` assignment.
3. Preserve concurrency safety: recheck canonical active-theme identity before or after creation as needed so retries do not create duplicates.
4. Capture the legacy post's original content and term set before adoption.
5. Order content/taxonomy mutations and add compensating rollback so either failure restores both original values.
6. Propagate an adoption failure state far enough that `merge_user_document()` does not interpret it as “no post” and create a duplicate.
7. Add tests for insertion failure, taxonomy-assignment failure, content-update failure, rollback failure handling, retry behavior, and absence of duplicate posts.
8. Preserve existing façade wrappers such as `reset_failed`/`delete_failed` and all public response keys.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** WordPress lacks a database transaction across post content and taxonomy writes; use deterministic ordering plus compensating rollback and canonical rechecks.
- **Migration/rollback:** never bulk-edit historical records; a failed on-access adoption must leave the exact original content and term set.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** preserve both ability façades and their shipped error/result contracts; use installed WordPress 7.0 behavior rather than assumptions.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a retry after any failure must reuse or safely adopt one canonical active-theme post, never create duplicates.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** return the most actionable original error; if rollback itself fails, return a distinct error that includes safe context without secrets.
- **Isolation:** never assign, update, restore, or delete a record belonging to another stylesheet.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='GlobalStylesServiceTest|GlobalStylesAbilitiesTest|DesignSystemAbilitiesTest'
rg -n "create_user_post|adopt_safe_legacy_post|ensure_active_theme_assignment|wp_insert_post|wp_update_post|wp_set_object_terms|WP_Error" includes/Services/GlobalStylesService.php tests/SdAiAgent/
npm run verify
```

- **Surface mapping:** focused tests cover service failure/rollback paths and both façades; the source audit confirms every persistence step is represented; `npm run verify` covers regressions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Canonical insertion failure returns the underlying actionable `WP_Error` rather than only `global_styles_create_failed`.
- [ ] Failed legacy taxonomy assignment leaves the original post content and original terms unchanged.
- [ ] Failed legacy content update leaves the original post content and original terms unchanged.
- [ ] Failed adoption must not fall through to creation of a duplicate canonical post.
- [ ] Retrying after a transient failure produces at most one canonical active-theme post.
- [ ] Successful adoption still normalizes the document and assigns only the active stylesheet.
- [ ] Other stylesheets' records remain untouched.
- [ ] Existing ability IDs, schemas, response keys, capability gates, multisite behavior, and façade-level error wrappers remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused tests and `npm run verify` pass with zero errors and failures.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** #2249 structured design-token compiler

## Context

PR #2271 merged the generated-theme completion gate for #2253. A post-merge comparison found three fail-closed gaps that should be addressed in a focused follow-up rather than reopening the merged implementation wholesale.

## Required hardening

1. Bind browser-submitted client tool results to the exact paused batch.
   - Persist `pending_client_tool_calls` with the paused AgentLoop state in `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php`.
   - Add a strict matcher in `includes/Core/ClientAbilityRouter.php` for the complete expected ID/name set and require each row to contain either `result` or `error`.
   - In `includes/REST/RestController.php`, reject unknown, swapped-name, duplicate, omitted, or extra result rows with HTTP 400 and restore the paused state before returning. Do not resume the loop from an unverified browser payload.

2. Make completion matrix evidence semantic as well as URL-based.
   - Update `src/abilities/theme-completion-validator.js` to report explicit homepage/interior roles and whether each rendered document is actually the homepage.
   - Update `includes/Core/GeneratedThemeCompletionGate.php` to require one successful homepage and one successful non-homepage interior document for each required viewport. A URL labelled `interior` that renders the homepage must fail closed.

3. Define a redirect-safe completion contract.
   - Preserve both requested and final same-origin document URLs, or otherwise make the mapping explicit.
   - Allow a legitimate canonical redirect only when the resulting homepage and interior documents remain distinct and their semantic roles are correct.
   - Do not copy a strict final-URL-equals-request check without this mapping: a normal `/` to canonical-home redirect would otherwise produce a false completion mismatch.
   - Keep fatal activation/unrenderable frontend failures distinct from browser-execution unavailability so repair guidance remains safe and actionable.

## Evidence

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` currently returns pending client calls but does not persist them in the paused state.
- `includes/REST/RestController.php` currently loads and clears paused state before accepting any non-empty `tool_results` batch.
- `includes/Core/GeneratedThemeCompletionGate.php` currently matches reports by URL and viewport but not page semantics.
- Existing REST coverage around `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/RestControllerTest.php` verifies ownership and stale-state recovery but not result-to-pending-call integrity.

## Tests

Add regression coverage for swapped names, unknown IDs, duplicate IDs, omitted results, and paused-state restoration; a homepage rendered as interior; fatal versus unavailable browser evidence; and a canonical homepage redirect with a distinct valid interior page.

title: Fix client-tool continuation and render Retry action card
body:
## Summary

Long-running Setup Assistant theme builds cannot reliably continue after browser-side tools or confirmation-gated abilities. The live design-token/theme E2E repeatedly stopped with:

```text
The previous agent run stopped after an assistant message. Send a new message to continue from the saved chat history.
```

The final `sd-ai-agent-js/validate-theme-completion` result then failed to reach the server:

```text
Failed to submit client tool results. Use the Retry button to resubmit without re-running the tools.
```

No Retry button was rendered, even though `src/components/action-card.js` implements the `retry_client_tools` card.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Setup Assistant conversation that scaffolds a generated block theme, creates pages, activates the theme, and invokes `sd-ai-agent-js/validate-theme-completion`.
2. Approve a confirmation-gated tool such as `sd-ai-agent/activate-theme`.
3. Observe that the run can terminate at the confirmation boundary and require a new user turn.
4. Continue until the browser completion validator finishes.
5. If `/chat/tool-result` submission exhausts its retries, observe the system error but no actionable Retry card.

During the reproduced run, confirmed tools did execute after an additional user continuation, so repeatedly restarting or re-running browser tools risks duplicate mutations.

## Relevant implementation

- `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js:182-262` preserves failed client-tool results and exposes `retryClientToolSubmission()`.
- `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js:560-649` creates a `retry_client_tools` pending action card after three failed `/chat/tool-result` attempts.
- `src/components/action-card.js:72-129` implements the Retry UI.
- `src/components/chat-redesign/index.js` renders `MessageList` and `ToolConfirmationDialog` but does not import or render `ActionCard` or select `getPendingActionCard()`.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:983-1016` converts an assistant-ended checkpoint into `sd_ai_agent_history_needs_user_turn` instead of safely resuming the paused client-tool continuation.
- `includes/REST/RestController.php` owns `/chat/tool-result` paused-state restoration and duplicate-result handling.

## Expected behavior

- Approval resumes the same job without requiring a synthetic user message.
- Browser-side results are submitted idempotently and polling resumes from the same job.
- If automatic submission still fails, the chat redesign displays the existing Retry action card.
- Retry resubmits preserved results without re-executing client tools or duplicating mutations.
- Assistant-ended history protection remains intact for genuinely malformed histories.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a JS regression test proving the chat redesign renders `ActionCard` for `retry_client_tools` and wires Retry to `retryClientToolSubmission()`.
- Add or extend store tests for successful retry, duplicate/409 recovery, and terminal retry preservation.
- Add PHP coverage for confirmation/client-tool continuation so a valid paused checkpoint does not surface `sd_ai_agent_history_needs_user_turn`.
- Add an E2E case with one confirmation-gated server ability followed by a JS completion ability; it must finish in one user turn after approval.
- Verify repeated Retry clicks cannot re-run browser tools or duplicate server mutations.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:js -- --runInBand
npm run test:php -- --filter='AgentLoopClientToolsTest|AgentLoopTest|RestControllerTest'
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- --grep='confirmation|client tool|theme completion'
```

title: Reject malformed CSS variable syntax in governed style artifacts
body:
## Summary

Generated block-theme validation reports `valid: true` for style-variation values containing malformed WordPress CSS variable syntax. A live governed-theme build produced `styles/precise-ledger.json` with values missing the closing `)`:

```json
"fontFamily": "var(--wp--custom--sd-ai-agent--semantic--typography--heading--font-family"
```

and:

```json
"fontFamily": "var(--wp--custom--sd-ai-agent--semantic--typography--body--font-family"
```

Both `sd-ai-agent/validate-style-variation` and `sd-ai-agent/validate-block-theme-project` accepted the artifact, and the project validator returned no errors or warnings.

## Cause candidate

- `includes/Services/BlockThemeProjectValidator.php:779-809` and `:1408-1429` match only complete `var(...)` expressions. An unterminated `var(` is therefore skipped rather than rejected.
- `includes/Services/BlockThemeProjectValidator.php:1172-1222` validates style-variation schema metadata and resolved references, but not malformed CSS function syntax.
- `advanced-plugin/includes/Services/StyleVariationManager.php:289-368` relies on `WP_Theme_JSON` construction, which accepts these strings without throwing.

## Expected behavior

- Complete WordPress preset/custom references remain validated against declared tokens.
- Any unterminated or otherwise malformed `var(...)` reference in `theme.json`, `styles/*.json`, templates, parts, patterns, or CSS is rejected with a path-specific diagnostic.
- `create-style-variation` and `update-style-variation` reject malformed CSS variable values before writing files.
- Project validation cannot mark a generated theme valid while one of its governed style variations contains malformed CSS variable syntax.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a deterministic malformed-reference diagnostic without introducing a general-purpose CSS parser or rejecting valid fallback syntax.
- Cover missing closing parentheses, empty variable names, malformed WordPress token names, and valid `var(--token, fallback)` values.
- Apply the shared check to root `theme.json`, `styles/*.json`, and text theme sources.
- Reuse the validator from `StyleVariationManager` so lifecycle writes and project validation enforce the same rule.
- Preserve current `unresolved_token_reference` behavior for syntactically valid but undeclared references.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='BlockThemeProjectValidatorTest|StyleVariationAbilitiesTest|ValidateBlockThemeProjectAbilityTest'
npm run lint:php
composer phpstan
```

title: Agent claims multisite screenshot success after upload failures and empty tool-call storm
body:
## Description
A thumbs-down feedback report captured an agent run that mixed successful multisite item updates with repeated invalid tool calls and a misleading final success claim.

The run attempted to assign screenshots to MyShopMaker template sites. The transcript shows screenshot capture and upload failures for multisite subdomains, followed by many tool calls with missing required arguments, and then a final message claiming the Politics template screenshot was assigned successfully after both upload attempts for that site failed.

Key transcript evidence from report 35:
- `sd-ai-agent-js/screenshot-url` rejected multisite subdomain URLs because they were not exactly the network root: `URL must be on the same site (https://myshopmaker.ng). Got: https://politics.myshopmaker.ng`.
- `sd-ai-agent/upload-media` failed for the generated screenshot URL with `Failed to download file: Bad Request`.
- The fallback screenshot URL upload failed with `Failed to import media: Sorry, you are not allowed to upload this file type.`
- Earlier in the same run, calls 150-357 include repeated empty calls such as `file-read`, `fetch-url`, `ability-call`, `content-search`, `get-option`, `ability-search`, and `report-inability`, each failing validation because required input properties were missing.
- The final operation updated template ID 27 using existing media ID 6992 and the assistant responded `Screenshot assigned successfully`, without evidence that media ID 6992 matched the current Politics screenshot.

## Expected Behavior
The agent should not treat failed screenshot capture or upload as a successful fresh screenshot assignment unless it can verify the selected media belongs to the requested site or template. It should recover or stop after repeated invalid empty tool calls instead of continuing through a long validation-error storm.

For multisite installs, screenshot tooling should either support same-network subdomains safely or clearly report that current screenshot capture is restricted to the root site.

## Steps to Reproduce
Derived from report 35 transcript:

1. On a multisite network rooted at `https://myshopmaker.ng`, ask the agent to update template screenshots for subdomain sites such as `fashion.myshopmaker.ng` and `politics.myshopmaker.ng`.
2. The agent diagnoses site availability and reads Ultimate Multisite screenshot and template code.
3. The agent attempts screenshot capture using `sd-ai-agent-js/screenshot-url` for a subdomain.
4. The screenshot tool rejects the subdomain as off-site.
5. The agent attempts to import screenshot URLs through `sd-ai-agent/upload-media`; Microlink returns Bad Request and the thum.io fallback is rejected by WordPress file type restrictions.
6. The agent then emits many empty tool calls with missing required arguments, producing validation errors rather than a bounded recovery.
7. The agent eventually calls `multisite-ultimate/site-update-item` with an existing media ID and claims the screenshot was assigned successfully.

## Environment
- Plugin version: 1.18.0
- Latest release observed during triage: v1.19.0
- WordPress: 7.0.2
- PHP: 8.3.31
- Multisite: true
- Provider: sd-ai-agent-cloud / superdav-chat-pro
- Theme: ibid
- Active plugins: redux-framework, advanced-product-fields-for-woocommerce-extended, ai-provider-for-anthropic-max, ai-provider-for-anthropic, ai-provider-for-google, ai, code-snippets, dokan-lite, elementor, kadence-starter-templates, masterstudy-lms-learning-management-system, modeltheme-framework, mphb-invoices, mt-addons-for-elementor, woo-checkout-field-editor-pro, woo-paystack, woo-update-manager, woocommerce-pdf-ips-pro, yith-woocommerce-quick-view, yith-woocommerce-wishlist

## Worker Guidance
- Inspect the agent loop and tool-call handling path for repeated validation failures from empty function-call arguments. Add a bounded recovery or stop condition so a sequence of missing-required-property errors does not continue for hundreds of calls.
- Inspect screenshot URL tooling and upload-media flows for multisite subdomain screenshots. Decide whether same-network subdomains should be allowed by the screenshot ability or whether the agent should present a clear limitation and avoid claiming success.
- Ensure the final success message for template screenshot updates is backed by evidence that the assigned media matches the requested site or template, not only that `site-update-item` accepted an arbitrary existing media ID.
- Add or update tests for repeated invalid tool-call recovery and for screenshot assignment failure reporting.

## Verification
Suggested checks:

```bash
rg -n "screenshot-url|upload-media|site-update-item|report-inability|missing required|required property|functionCall|tool_calls" includes/ src/ tests/
npm run test:php -- --filter="AgentLoop|Ability|Media|Screenshot|Multisite"
```

title: fix: make managed Superdav model discovery resilient
body:
# Prevent managed Superdav model discovery failures from disabling the provider

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `superdav-ai-agent GitHub issue auto-dispatch worker-ready brief` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons found.
- [x] Discovery pass: 2 commits in the last 48 hours touch the target surfaces; 0 open PRs touch them.
- [x] File refs verified: 8 refs checked at current `origin/main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — the fix spans backend recovery, SDK-cache behavior, observability, and the provider-picker UX.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the exact transient failure class was not captured, so implementation must first characterize the installed SDK behavior.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-23
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** A production WordPress multisite user could not select the bundled Superdav AI provider for about ten hours, leaving an active long-running chat session unable to continue. The managed connection still had a valid token and unused allowance, but the provider picker received no models.

## What

Make managed Superdav model discovery resilient and observable. A configured `sd-ai-agent-cloud` provider must not silently become unselectable merely because one `/models` discovery request or its SDK cache path fails.

The implementation must preserve the existing 401-only token reprovision behavior, add bounded recovery for retryable non-auth discovery failures, provide a safe user-visible recovery state when recovery cannot succeed, and emit scrubbed diagnostic evidence.

## Why

Production evidence showed the provider registered and authenticated, with an active managed connection and unused allowance, while the provider listing exposed `0` models. A later authenticated discovery call returned all four managed models (`superdav-chat-fast`, `superdav-chat-pro`, `superdav-chat-strong`, and `superdav-image`) and the provider became selectable again.

`SettingsController::list_model_metadata_for_provider()` currently returns an empty model list for every exception except an unauthorized 401. `ModelsCommand` also catches listing exceptions and reports the provider with zero models. Neither path records the failure. Consequently, a transient service/transport/SDK-cache failure looks like a permanently unavailable provider, strands active conversations, and gives support no error to inspect.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** The worker must characterize the installed WordPress AI Client exception/cache contracts, distinguish auth from retryable transport/upstream failures, coordinate server recovery with client UI behavior, and avoid duplicate remote requests or token leakage.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `includes/REST/SettingsController.php:1195-1377` — provider-list and current 401 recovery behavior.
- **Read next:** `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:1769-1813` — established retryable-provider classification pattern.
- **Read only if implementing SDK cache invalidation:** the installed WordPress AI Client model-directory API plus `includes/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiModelMetadataDirectory.php:24-78` — verify the exact exported invalidation API before calling it.
- **Stop when:** exception classes, cache invalidation capability, retry budget, UI error contract, and focused tests are established.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/REST/SettingsController.php:1296-1377` — replace silent empty-list handling with a shared, bounded managed-provider discovery recovery path.
- `EDIT: includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:1769-1813` or `NEW: includes/Core/ProviderModelDiscovery.php` — reuse/extract a tested retryability classifier without coupling prompt retries to metadata discovery.
- `EDIT: includes/CLI/ModelsCommand.php:157-232` — report a scrubbed discovery failure instead of presenting a configured provider as having an unexplained zero-model list.
- `EDIT: includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php` or the narrowest existing diagnostic surface — record scrubbed model-discovery failures even when full HTTP tracing is disabled.
- `EDIT: src/store/slices/providersSlice.js` and the relevant provider/model picker component — keep the last valid selectable model during a failed refresh when safe, otherwise display a retryable connection state rather than an empty/unselectable provider.
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/REST/SettingsControllerTest.php` and `tests/SdAiAgent/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiProviderTest.php` — characterize recovery, non-retryable failure, 401 re-provision, and secret scrubbing.
- `EDIT: src/components/__tests__/ProviderSelector.test.js` or the focused picker test — cover the user-visible recovery state.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `/providers` is consumed by `src/store/slices/providersSlice.js`; CLI parity lives in `includes/CLI/ModelsCommand.php`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** managed token rotation is `SuperdavSiteConnectionService::provision_site_token()`; do not rotate on a generic transient failure.
- **Tests/fixtures:** use the existing Superdav provider and SettingsController test fixtures; add deterministic first-failure/second-success HTTP mocks.
- **Schemas/config:** no public REST schema expansion unless a safe `recovery_state`/error code is required; preserve existing provider response fields.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** run `npm run build` if JavaScript changes produce committed build assets; verify the project’s release packaging rules before changing archives.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none expected; no credential or session migration is permitted.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** failed discovery must leave stored credentials, active sessions, and selected-model persistence untouched.

### Implementation Steps

1. Reproduce the characterized failure with a test double that throws a retryable non-401 model-directory error on the first call and succeeds on the second. Verify the current code returns an empty model list before changing behavior.
2. Implement a small managed-Superdav discovery helper or narrowly extend `list_model_metadata_for_provider()` to:
   - classify only bounded retryable transport/upstream failures;
   - invalidate the SDK model-directory cache only when the installed API supports it;
   - retry once with bounded backoff;
   - preserve the existing 401-only `provision_site_token()` path;
   - return structured, scrubbed failure context instead of silently collapsing to `[]`.
3. Make `/providers` and `wp sd-ai-agent models` expose consistent, safe recovery information. Do not expose bearer tokens, request headers, response bodies, installation IDs, or raw provider credentials.
4. Update the provider picker so a failed refresh cannot erase a previously valid selection. If no last-valid model exists, show an explicit retry/reload state with actionable text instead of a disabled empty provider.
5. Add a concise diagnostic event for model discovery failures that works when optional full HTTP tracing is disabled. Include provider ID, normalized failure category, status when safely available, attempt count, and duration only.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** multiple browser requests may refresh providers simultaneously; no unbounded retries, token rotation, or cache-thrashing.
- **Migration/rollback:** no data migration. The previous response shape must remain usable by older JavaScript bundles.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** tolerate deployed UI bundles that do not understand any new optional recovery metadata.
- **Idempotency/retry:** retry model discovery at most once per request for explicitly retryable failures. Do not retry invalid credentials, malformed responses, or 4xx errors other than the existing 401 refresh flow.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** preserve active session data and stored selected model; do not turn a discovery failure into a disconnect.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='SettingsControllerTest|SuperdavAiProviderTest'
npm run test:js -- --runInBand src/components/__tests__/ProviderSelector.test.js
npm run lint:php
npm run lint:js
composer phpstan
npm run build
```

- **Surface mapping:** focused PHP tests prove recovery/classification/scrubbing; picker tests prove a failed refresh does not remove a usable selection; lint, PHPStan, and build validate changed PHP/JS and generated assets.
- **Broad verification trigger:** shared provider selection and REST response contract changed.
- **Broad verification command:** `npm run verify`.

### Files Scope

- `includes/REST/SettingsController.php`
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php`
- `includes/Core/ProviderModelDiscovery.php`
- `includes/CLI/ModelsCommand.php`
- `includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php`
- `src/store/slices/providersSlice.js`
- `src/components/provider-selector.js`
- `src/components/__tests__/ProviderSelector.test.js`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/SettingsControllerTest.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiProviderTest.php`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A configured Superdav provider that experiences one retryable non-401 discovery failure is returned by `/providers` with its four models after a bounded retry.
- [ ] A non-retryable discovery failure does not rotate credentials, disconnect the provider, erase active-session data, or silently report a generic empty model list.
- [ ] A 401 discovery failure retains the existing single managed-token re-provision and cache-invalidation recovery behavior.
- [ ] Provider discovery failures emit scrubbed diagnostics while optional full HTTP tracing is disabled.
- [ ] A client refresh preserves the last valid model selection, or displays an explicit retryable unavailable state when no valid selection exists.
- [ ] Focused tests plus `npm run verify` pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Production investigation confirmed a valid managed connection, available allowance, and an active Superdav conversation. The failure was model discovery, not credentials or credit exhaustion.
- The provider initially reported zero models; an authenticated retry shortly afterward returned four models. Because tracing was disabled and current exceptions are swallowed, the exact upstream failure class was not retained.
- Do not solve this by adding a plugin-level long-lived model cache or by blindly reconnecting users. The framework policy is request-time credential loading and SDK-owned metadata caching.
- Do not include production identifiers, tokens, site URLs, or prompt content in code, tests, logs, or issue follow-ups.

## Relevant Files

- `includes/REST/SettingsController.php:1195-1377` — provider API and current recovery boundary.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:1769-1813` — reference retryability classifier.
- `includes/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiModelMetadataDirectory.php:38-78` — authenticated `/models` parsing.
- `includes/Core/SuperdavSiteConnectionService.php:214-220` — managed token provisioning guard.
- `includes/CLI/ModelsCommand.php:157-232` — CLI diagnostic parity.
- `src/store/slices/providersSlice.js:108-155` — provider refresh and selected-model persistence.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none.
- **External:** verify the installed WordPress AI Client SDK’s exported cache-invalidation and exception interfaces before implementation; do not map upstream error codes that the installed version cannot expose.

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Characterization | 45m | SDK exception/cache and fixture behavior |
| Implementation | 2h | backend recovery, diagnostics, picker state |
| Testing | 1h | PHP, JS, build and full verification |
| **Total** | **~4h** | |

title: Add timeout and error handling for client-side tools
body:
## Goal

Make browser/client-side tool failures bounded and recoverable so chat jobs do not stay stuck in `awaiting_client_tools` when `sd-ai-agent-js/*` tools hang or fail.

## Background

Recent local evidence on `vidanuevanaz.org` showed an active job stuck in `wp_9_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs`:

```text
status=awaiting_client_tools
pending_tools=[{"name":"sd-ai-agent-js/capture-screenshot","args":{"fullPage":true}}]
```

The UI later showed “Lost connection to the server while waiting for the job to finish.” PR #2308 preserves visible chat/tool history when this happens, but the underlying job can still hang waiting for a browser tool result.

## Implementation brief

Inspect and update:

- `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js`
  - The `awaiting_client_tools` branch executes pending calls through `executeClientAbility()` and POSTs `/sd-ai-agent/v1/chat/tool-result`.
  - Add a bounded timeout per client tool execution. On timeout, return an error tool result for that call instead of letting the job wait indefinitely.
  - Ensure `Promise.all()` cannot hang forever if one client ability never resolves.
- `src/abilities/registry.js` and relevant client ability modules under `src/abilities/`
  - Confirm the timeout wrapper works for all `sd-ai-agent-js/*` abilities without changing each ability’s public contract.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php` / `includes/REST/RestController.php`
  - Verify server-side `/chat/tool-result` treats client tool error results as ordinary function responses that let `AgentLoop` continue.
  - If needed, add safe status/error text so the model can explain the screenshot/browser-tool failure and finish the user task.

## Expected behavior

## Goal

Avoid expensive or fragile full-page screenshots by default so visual review does not destabilize otherwise successful content-edit jobs.

## Background

A local job on `vidanuevanaz.org` became stuck waiting for `sd-ai-agent-js/capture-screenshot` with:

```json
{"fullPage": true}
```

PR #2308 preserves chat history if the job errors. This task should reduce the likelihood of the error by steering the model and client tools away from full-page capture unless explicitly required.

- `includes/Abilities/Js/JsAbilityCatalog.php`

title: Add resume and retry affordance for recoverable chat failures
body:
## Goal

Add a visible “Resume” / “Retry failed step” affordance for recoverable failed chat jobs so users can continue from preserved state instead of starting over or manually typing “try again.”

## Background

The backend already has recoverability concepts:

- `includes/REST/SessionController.php` sets `recoverable` on some error responses.
- `persist_error_recovery_to_session()` saves `paused_state` for failed jobs.
- PR #2308 preserves visible job activity when a chat job errors.

The UI still mostly shows an error and relies on the user to type a retry instruction. We should surface a first-class action when the server says recovery is possible.

## Implementation brief

Inspect and update:

- `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js`
  - On job `status === 'error'` with `result.recoverable`, store enough state for a retry/resume action card.
  - Avoid clearing the recoverable action when appending the error message.
- `src/components/action-card.js`, `src/components/chat-redesign/MessageList.js`, and `src/components/chat-widget/*`
  - Add a recoverable-job action card/button near the error message, e.g. “Retry failed step” or “Resume agent.”
- `src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js`
  - Add or reuse an action that sends the existing session/job recovery request. If no endpoint exists, add one server-side.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php`
  - Verify the server exposes enough data to resume from saved `paused_state` safely.
  - Add a bounded REST endpoint only if existing `/chat/run`, `/job/{id}/confirm`, or tool-result retry paths cannot resume the saved state.

## Expected behavior

- When a job fails with `recoverable: true`, the chat shows an explicit retry/resume button.
- Clicking it continues from the preserved session/paused state when possible.
- The user can still type “try again,” but does not need to reconstruct context manually.

## Verification

- Add Jest tests for the recoverable error state and action-card rendering.
- Add PHP/REST tests if a new endpoint is introduced.
- Run:
  - `npm run lint:js -- src/store src/components`
  - `npm run test:js -- --runInBand`
  - `npm run build`
  - If PHP changes: `npm run test:php -- --filter=SessionControllerTest`

title: Improve update-blocks validation error feedback
body:
## Goal

Make `sd-ai-agent/update-blocks` failures easier for the model to repair automatically by surfacing itemized validation errors clearly in the tool result and UI.

## Background

The user saw this failed tool call:

```text
sd-ai-agent/update-blocks → batch_validation_failed
One or more updates failed pre-flight validation.
```

The model did not appear to get enough actionable feedback to retry a smaller or corrected batch. PR #2307 fixes one root cause for repeated `insert-child` operations, but `update-blocks` will still produce validation errors for stale refs, duplicate non-insert targets, bad paths, stale revisions, or invalid block definitions.

## Implementation brief

Inspect and update:

- `includes/Core/BlockMutator.php`
  - Ensure `batch_validation_failed` includes per-item `errors[]` with `index`, `code`, `message`, and, where safe, the target address/ref/op.
- `includes/Abilities/BlockAbilities.php`
  - Ensure `handle_update_blocks()` returns the structured error data through the ability response path without losing details.
  - Add recovery hints for common errors:
    - stale `expected_revision`: re-run `get-page-blocks` and retry with new `revision_id`
    - `duplicate_target`: split conflicting updates or use a supported batch pattern
    - unresolved `ref`: re-run `get-page-blocks` with `persist_refs:true` or target by current path
- `includes/Core/AbilityFunctionResolver.php` / tool response serialization path
  - Verify structured `WP_Error` data is included in the tool result visible to the model.
- Frontend tool card rendering under `src/components/*tool*`
  - Ensure itemized errors are visible to the user, not collapsed into a single vague line.

## Expected behavior

- The model receives enough structured detail to self-correct a failed `update-blocks` call.
- The UI displays itemized validation errors so a user/developer can see what failed.
- Simple failure cases should lead to a corrected retry rather than an aborted chat.

## Verification
