## Description
A thumbs-down report from a multisite install says many tool calls failed while the agent was asked to make the home page bilingual. The transcript confirms repeated tool errors during the edit flow, including a failed `update-blocks` pre-flight validation, four `sd-ai-agent/prompt` calls failing because no text-generation model was found, and a blocked internal fetch.

This looks actionable because the agent had already loaded and modified page blocks, then continued into fallback/verification work that produced multiple recoverable but user-visible failures instead of completing the bilingual home-page task cleanly.

## Expected Behavior
The agent should update the requested home-page text bilingually, use valid block-update payloads, avoid unavailable prompt/model paths, and report any remaining limitations clearly without cascading through repeated failing tool calls.

1. On the reported site, ask: `Make sure all the text no the home page is bilingual`.

title: Expose a versioned server-side customer-agent runtime
body:
## Objective

Expose a stable, versioned, server-side customer-agent runtime that another trusted WordPress plugin can use without coupling to Superdav's anonymous browser REST routes or internal `SessionController` job representation.

The first consumer is Ultimate Multisite Support Tickets: it must retain ownership of the customer transcript and routing state while Superdav executes constrained asynchronous AI turns.

## Pre-flight evidence

- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:1770-1947` currently creates anonymous transient sessions, queues jobs, and polls results inside a REST controller.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:1837-1866` shows the reusable job inputs, but those inputs are represented as controller-private arrays.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:1931-1944` deletes terminal jobs on first successful/error poll, which is unsuitable for retry-safe plugin-to-plugin reconciliation.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:495-552` already applies and clears request-scoped anonymous ability and knowledge restrictions.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/PublicChatControllerTest.php:88-201` is the regression reference for anonymous job isolation and token-scoped polling.
- `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no related open PR and no recently merged implementation for this contract.

## Scope

### Contract

- Add a public PHP interface/service for trusted same-install consumers. Choose the final class/file names to match repository conventions; likely locations are `includes/Contracts/` and/or `includes/Services/`.
- Provide explicit capability discovery, including a semantic contract version and feature flags, so consumers fail closed when an older/incompatible Superdav version is active.
- Support these operations with typed array DTOs or value objects and stable `WP_Error` codes:
  - create or recover a runtime conversation for an external integration/session key;
  - enqueue one customer turn with an external idempotency key;
  - inspect a job without consuming its terminal result;
  - cancel an in-flight job;
  - close/purge a runtime conversation.
- Return opaque Superdav conversation/job identifiers, normalized statuses (`queued`, `processing`, `complete`, `failed`, `cancelled`), sanitized reply/error data, model/provider identifiers, iteration count, and token usage when available.

### Runtime behavior

- Extract/reuse the execution mechanics currently embedded in `SessionController`; do not make the consumer call anonymous REST endpoints or mint/publicly expose browser tokens.
- Keep Superdav responsible for model execution and constrained runtime history only. Do not duplicate or become the system of record for Support Tickets' customer transcript.
- Make enqueue idempotent for `(integration_key, external_session_id, external_message_id)`. Concurrent retries must resolve to the same job and must not bill or answer twice.
- Persist enough job state to reconcile after transient expiry, process restart, delayed cron/loopback execution, or a consumer polling retry. Terminal status must remain readable for a documented retention period and polling must not delete it.
- Reuse `ActiveJobRepository`, checkpoints, and existing provider retry/error classification where appropriate rather than creating a parallel loop implementation.
- Ensure cancellation prevents a late result from being treated as deliverable. Document races where provider work cannot be physically stopped.
- Bound history, message length, runtime duration, and iterations. Return a stable timeout/failure state rather than leaving jobs permanently `processing`.

### Trust and safety

- Require a registered integration key and an enabled customer-agent profile; arbitrary request data must not be able to select unrestricted agents, providers, tools, collections, system instructions, or client-side abilities.
- Apply the same fail-closed ability and collection gates used by anonymous public chat. Meta-tools, browser/client tools, mutations, and attachments remain unavailable unless a later explicit policy adds them.
- Sanitize customer-visible errors with the existing error-detail protections; never expose paths, stack traces, credentials, prompts, or raw provider payloads.
- Do not add a new unauthenticated REST surface for this issue. If an authenticated REST adapter is needed for tests/admin diagnostics, require an explicit capability and nonce.
- Emit privacy-safe lifecycle events keyed by hashed/opaque integration, session, and job identifiers; do not log message bodies.
- Preserve all existing `/public-chat/*` behavior and tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test consumer can discover the contract version, create/recover a conversation, enqueue a turn, poll it repeatedly through a terminal state, and close it without using public-chat tokens or accessing controller-private arrays.
- Repeating or racing the same external message id returns the same job and executes one agent turn.
- A different integration/session cannot inspect or cancel the job.
- Terminal results survive more than one read and remain recoverable when the transient cache is unavailable.
- Expired/stuck jobs become a deterministic failed/timeout state; cancelled jobs cannot later publish a successful reply.
- The runtime rejects unknown integrations, disabled profiles, unapproved abilities/collections, client tools, attachments, and caller-supplied system prompts.
- Existing public-chat endpoint behavior remains backward compatible.
- Public API and lifecycle semantics are documented for plugin authors.

## Reference pattern

Follow the existing public-chat job construction/status lifecycle and `AgentLoop` anonymous-gate cleanup, but extract shared service primitives rather than calling REST callbacks or duplicating their private arrays.

## Files to modify

- `includes/REST/SessionController.php` — extract/reuse public-chat job orchestration instead of duplicating it.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — constrained execution and cleanup pattern.
- `includes/Models/ActiveJobRepository.php` and its row/schema collaborators — durable job lifecycle reference.
- `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php` — exact anonymous ability allowlist enforcement.
- `includes/Abilities/KnowledgeAbilities.php` — collection isolation.
- `includes/Core/ConversationDisplaySanitizer.php` — customer-safe history/reply serialization.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/PublicChatControllerTest.php` — preserve browser public-chat behavior.
- Add focused service/contract tests under `tests/SdAiAgent/Services/` or the nearest matching namespace.

## Verification

- Run the focused new runtime test class.
- Run `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter PublicChatControllerTest`.
- Run relevant `AgentLoop`, `ActiveJobRepository`, `ToolDiscovery`, and `KnowledgeAbilities` test classes.
- Run `composer test`, `composer phpstan`, and `composer phpcs` (or the repository-equivalent scripts if names differ on current `main`).

## Dependencies and delivery notes

- No predecessor issue; this is a foundation task and can run in parallel with Support Tickets' routing-schema foundation.
- This contract intentionally does not provision the managed support profile; that is a separate follow-up.
- Target workload: `tier:thinking`, high priority, approximately 4 hours.

title: Add a safely managed customer-support agent profile
body:
## Objective

Add a managed customer-support agent profile that trusted integrations can provision idempotently and execute through the versioned customer-agent runtime from #2320, with a customer-specific prompt pipeline and immutable safety boundaries.

This must make the selected support agent's instructions authoritative without allowing the customer browser or consuming plugin to widen tools, collections, or privileges.

## Pre-flight evidence

- `includes/Models/Agent.php:1-18` defines custom agents with prompts, models, Tier-1 tools, greetings, and iteration settings.
- `includes/Models/Agent.php:349-394` maps a selected agent's prompt to `agent_system_prompt` and applies model/tool overrides.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:358-369` can use `agent_system_prompt`, but `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:462-468` locks any explicit `system_instruction` instead.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:1850-1865` passes both `agent_id` and a hard-coded public `system_instruction`; the locked instruction therefore bypasses the selected agent prompt.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:1951-1966` contains the current fixed documentation-assistant prompt.
- `includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php:108-128` appends global advanced-companion, memory, and skill context, which must not leak into a customer support profile.
- `includes/Abilities/PublicChatSetupAbilities.php:27-28` correctly constrains the existing public setup path to `sd-ai-agent/knowledge-search` only.
- Closed #2176 implemented anonymous-safe gating, while closed #2190 was a production docs-assistant setup task; neither provides a reusable managed support-profile lifecycle.

## Scope

### Managed profile lifecycle

- Extend the #2320 runtime with an idempotent `ensure_profile`/status operation keyed by a stable integration key such as `ultimate-multisite-support-tickets` and a profile/spec version.
- Reuse the existing agent model where appropriate, but add explicit managed ownership metadata rather than guessing ownership from an agent name or numeric ID.
- Define per-field ownership:
  - integration-managed safety envelope, allowed ability set, allowed knowledge collections, profile schema version, and customer mode cannot be widened in the normal agent editor;
  - operator-managed provider/model, greeting/avatar/brand copy, approved collections, and bounded generation settings survive repeated provisioning unless the operator requests reset;
  - document any fields intentionally reset when the integration's safety spec version increases.
- Return a customer-safe health summary: profile key/version, enabled/ready state, missing provider/model/collection reasons, safe capability list, and drift status. Never return raw prompts, credentials, or private collection contents to the consumer.
- Support disable, re-provision, and remove semantics without deleting unrelated custom agents or conversations.

### Customer-specific prompt policy

- Introduce an explicit prompt composition path for customer agents. Required precedence:
  1. immutable Superdav customer-safety envelope;
  2. managed profile/support instructions;
  3. approved knowledge/citation guidance;
  4. bounded, sanitized request context from the trusted consumer.
- Do not use the current locked hard-coded prompt in a way that discards the profile prompt.
- Do not inherit global site-agent memories, skill indexes, advanced-companion instructions, admin page context, or normal authenticated agent defaults.
- The default support profile should:
  - identify itself as an AI support assistant;
  - answer from approved Ultimate Multisite documentation/knowledge and cite source titles/URLs when present;
  - say when evidence is insufficient rather than inventing an answer;
  - invite/escalate to a human through a structured handoff signal rather than claiming a person has been contacted;
  - never claim access to private account/site data, billing, licenses, admin, files, database, users, settings, WP-CLI, memory, or internal REST tools.
- Return structured handoff intent/reason separately from display text when the model requests a human, detects account/private-data needs, or cannot answer safely.

### Tool and knowledge policy

- Default to `sd-ai-agent/knowledge-search` only. Reject meta-tools, client/browser tools, attachments, mutations, memory, skills, internal REST dispatch, and generic CLI/file/database abilities.
- Compute effective abilities and collections as the intersection of Superdav's immutable customer-safe set, the managed profile policy, and current operator-approved resources. A consumer request can narrow this set but never widen it.
- Validate referenced collections exist and are public/customer-approved before marking the profile ready.
- Keep public anonymous-chat behavior backward compatible; migrate it to the shared prompt/profile primitives only when tests prove no behavior regression.

## Acceptance criteria

- Provisioning the same integration/profile spec repeatedly yields one managed profile and preserves documented operator-owned fields.
- A safety-spec upgrade updates only managed fields and reports drift/reset actions.
- The executed system instruction contains the safety envelope and selected support instructions, but no global memory, skill index, advanced-companion, or admin instructions.
- Attempts to add a privileged tool/collection through consumer input or the generic agent editor fail closed.
- A missing/disabled provider, model, or collection produces a precise non-secret readiness error.
- Runtime results can include a normalized handoff signal without relying on phrase matching in generated prose.
- Existing custom agents and `/public-chat/*` flows continue to work.

## Reference pattern

Follow `Agent` model CRUD/DTO conventions and `PublicChatSetupAbilities` fail-closed knowledge policy, while adding explicit managed-field ownership and a customer-only prompt composer instead of overloading the global prompt builder.

## Files to modify

- `includes/Models/Agent.php` and `includes/Models/DTO/AgentRow.php` — existing agent configuration and persistence.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — current prompt override precedence and anonymous gates.
- `includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php` — reference only; customer mode must not append private/global context.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php` — replace the hard-coded selected-agent bypass with shared customer prompt primitives where appropriate.
- `includes/Abilities/PublicChatSetupAbilities.php` — safe knowledge-only setup reference.
- `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php` and `includes/Abilities/KnowledgeAbilities.php` — effective policy enforcement.
- Add focused managed-profile and customer-prompt tests under `tests/SdAiAgent/Models/`, `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/`, and/or `tests/SdAiAgent/Services/`.

## Verification

- Run the new managed-profile lifecycle and prompt-composition tests.
- Run `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter 'AgentTest|AgentLoopTest|SystemInstructionBuilderTest|PublicChatControllerTest|PublicChatSetupAbilitiesTest|ToolDiscoveryTest|KnowledgeAbilitiesTest'`.
- Run the repository PHPStan and PHPCS commands and the full PHP test suite.

## Dependencies and delivery notes

- Blocked by #2320; implement against its final contract rather than introducing a second integration API.
- This is distinct from closed #2190: that issue configured one production docs embed, while this issue provides a reusable, versioned, safely managed support profile.
- Target workload: `tier:thinking`, high priority, approximately 4 hours.

title: Review followup: PR #2325 — GH#2321: add safely managed customer-support agent profile
body:
<!-- aidevops:generator=review-followup source_pr=2325 fingerprint=source-pr-2325 -->
## Unaddressed review bot suggestions

PR #2325 was merged with unaddressed review bot feedback. Each comment
below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline
review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was
flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's
GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether
the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue
with a wontfix rationale.

**Source PR:** https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/pull/2325

---

### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule)

This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched
directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false
premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without
measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `AGENTS.md`
"AI-Generated Issue Quality"). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting.

You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back
to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do
analysis.

#### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue

1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below).
2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that
   line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section
   isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a
   comment in this shape:

   > **Premise falsified.** \<what the bot claimed\>. \<what the code
   > actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>.
   > Not acting.

   No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next
   session reading this thread and the noise filter.

#### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR

1. Verify the bot's premise as above.
2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement.
3. Open a PR with `Resolves #<this-issue-number>` in the body
   (use THIS issue's number, not the source PR's) so merge auto-closes it.
4. Follow the normal Lifecycle Gate (brief, tests, review-bot-gate,
   merge, postflight).

#### Outcome C — Premise correct but approach is a genuine judgment call

Only use this path if you reach it after Outcomes A and B don't apply:
the bot's finding is real, but the fix requires a decision that is
architectural, policy, breaking-change, or otherwise genuinely outside
what you can resolve autonomously. In that case, post a **decision
comment** with exactly these fields:

- **Premise check:** one line, confirming the finding is real.
- **Analysis:** 2-4 bullets on the trade-offs.
- **Recommended path:** the option you would take if the decision were
  yours, with rationale.
- **Specific question:** the single decision the human needs to make
  (yes/no or pick-one, not open-ended).

Then apply `needs-maintainer-review` and stop. The human wakes up to a

title: update-blocks pre-flight validation lacks actionable recovery details
body:
## Description
A thumbs-down report says the agent could not make simple page updates after it created a site-wide palette from a blue/green logo. The transcript shows the agent successfully loaded design guidance, found logo media, updated theme JSON presets, inspected page blocks for page ID 8, and then failed twice when calling `sd-ai-agent/update-blocks`.

The failing tool responses were both: `One or more updates failed pre-flight validation.` The transcript does not include a more actionable validation detail, so the agent had no clear recovery path for the page update.

## Expected Behavior
When `update-blocks` rejects a page update during pre-flight validation, the agent should receive enough structured detail to recover safely, such as the failed operation index, target block ref/path, rejected attribute, expected schema, or remediation guidance. If the proposed block update is invalid, the agent should be able to adjust the update rather than retrying the same failing operation.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On a multisite WordPress install using the Astra theme, ask the agent to create a color palette based on an existing blue/green logo and apply it to the theme/pages.
2. The agent loads `design-system-aesthetics`, lists logo media, and calls `sd-ai-agent/get-global-styles` with `site_url` set to `https://vidanuevanaz.org/wp`, which fails because no site matches that URL.
3. The agent calls `sd-ai-agent/theme-json-presets` with `action: update`, which succeeds.
4. The agent inspects page ID 8 with `get-page-blocks` and `get-post`.
5. The agent calls `sd-ai-agent/update-blocks` twice against expected revision 2629 to update button/group attributes.
6. Both `update-blocks` calls fail with only `One or more updates failed pre-flight validation.`

- Plugin version: 1.19.0

- Multisite: true

title: Account page: securely redeem Superdav credit coupons
body:
## Problem

Users need to redeem Superdav AI coupon codes for credits from the account settings page. The current account endpoint only reads account status and has no redemption flow.

## Scope

Implement a secure, explicit coupon-redemption action that submits a code server-to-server to the managed Superdav AI service, then refreshes and displays the authoritative wallet balance. Coupon values are sensitive entitlement data and must not be retained after the request.

## Files and reference patterns

- `includes/Core/SuperdavSiteConnectionService.php`: add a narrowly scoped redemption method beside `refresh_account_status()`, using the stored site bearer token only in server-side request headers.
- `includes/REST/SettingsController.php`: register a dedicated, capability-gated redemption route beside `/superdav-account`; validate a JSON `coupon_code` parameter and return only sanitized account status.
- `src/settings-page/superdav-account-manager.js`: add an accessible coupon input, submit action, pending state, and success/error notices; clear the input after every response.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/SettingsControllerTest.php`: cover permission, validation, service success, invalid/expired/already-redeemed responses, upstream failure, token secrecy, and refreshed wallet output.
- `src/settings-page/__tests__/superdav-account-manager.test.js`: cover validation, submit state, input clearing, success balance update, and safe error rendering.

## Required service contract

Confirm the managed service's documented redemption endpoint, request schema, idempotency behaviour, and error codes before coding. Do not guess an endpoint path, map undocumented error codes, or implement local coupon validation. The service must make the redemption atomic and return the updated safe wallet summary.

## Security requirements

- Require `manage_options`, a valid WordPress REST nonce, and the real current user context.
- Send the coupon and bearer token only in the server-to-server request body/header. Never include either in query strings, options, transients, REST responses, audit logs, PHP errors, browser analytics, or debug notices.
- Do not persist coupon codes, redemption attempts, or raw service error payloads. Log only a redacted outcome if operational auditing is required.
- Treat duplicate submit/retry behaviour as an upstream idempotency concern; disable the submit control while a request is active.

## Acceptance criteria

- An administrator can redeem a valid code from the account page and immediately sees the updated wallet with a fresh timestamp.
- Invalid, expired, already-redeemed, and unavailable-service responses are actionable but reveal no coupon, token, or raw upstream payload.
- The code field is cleared after both success and failure.
- Non-admin REST requests are rejected, and a plugin agent cannot invoke the route through `wp-rest/execute`.
- The existing balance auto-refresh and manual refresh continue to work after redemption.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter=SettingsControllerTest
npm run test:js -- superdav-account-manager.test.js
npm run lint
composer phpstan
npm run build
```

Use a disposable service test coupon. Verify the updated balance through the account page and a fresh account-status request, without printing the coupon or any credential in terminal, test, or PR output.

title: Account page: add dedicated credit purchase and payment-method actions
body:
## Problem

The Superdav AI account page exposes **Add credits**, **Manage payment methods**, and **Open account portal**, but all three currently use one generic portal URL. Users cannot reliably start the specific billing action they selected from WordPress.

## Scope

Add dedicated, service-issued action URLs for purchasing credits and managing payment methods. Payment details must remain entirely in the external Superdav AI billing service; WordPress must never collect, proxy, store, log, or return card or bank data.

## Files and reference patterns

- `includes/Core/SuperdavSiteConnectionService.php`: extend `sanitize_remote_metadata()` and `get_status()` using the existing `account_portal_url` allowlist and secret-query-key protection as the reference pattern.
- `includes/REST/SettingsController.php`: keep `GET|POST /sd-ai-agent/v1/superdav-account` admin-gated and return only sanitized action metadata.
- `src/settings-page/superdav-account-manager.js`: replace the three shared generic links with action-specific buttons; use a single generic portal fallback only when a dedicated URL is unavailable.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/SettingsControllerTest.php`: add safe-metadata and secret-query rejection coverage.
- `src/settings-page/__tests__/superdav-account-manager.test.js`: verify dedicated URLs and the fallback rendering.

## Required service contract

Before implementing the UI, confirm the managed account response provides, or can provide, non-secret HTTPS URLs such as `purchase_credits_url` and `payment_methods_url`. Do not fabricate paths or append query parameters to `account_portal_url`. If the service cannot provide these URLs, retain the generic portal CTA and document the upstream dependency in the implementation PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- The page renders **Add credits** only from the service-provided purchase URL and **Manage payment methods** only from the service-provided payment-method URL.
- A generic **Open account portal** action remains available when the generic URL is safe.
- Every remote URL is sanitized with the same scheme/host validation and secret-query-key rejection used for the existing portal URL; URLs containing access tokens, API keys, or other credential-like query keys are omitted from REST responses and persisted metadata.
- No payment form, card field, coupon field, billing address, or payment response is added to WordPress.
- Missing dedicated URLs produce an accurate generic-portal fallback without dead buttons or misleading labels.
- All routes remain protected by the existing `manage_options` permission callback.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter=SettingsControllerTest
npm run test:js -- superdav-account-manager.test.js
npm run lint
composer phpstan
npm run build
```

Manually test with a service response containing distinct safe URLs, then with each URL absent or containing a blocked query key. Confirm the browser opens only the expected external URL and the REST response never contains service tokens.

title: Account page: show credit activity, usage, and expiry
body:
## Problem

The account page currently shows only a balance snapshot and plan. Users cannot understand recent credit purchases, coupon grants, consumption, pending adjustments, expiring promotional credits, or when their balance will change.

## Scope

Add a read-only account activity and credit-lifecycle section backed by a minimal, sanitized managed-service response. This is an observability feature only: WordPress must not become a billing ledger or cache sensitive financial records beyond a short-lived display response.

## Files and reference patterns

- `includes/Core/SuperdavSiteConnectionService.php`: extend the safe remote metadata contract using explicit allowlists, scalar validation, and timestamp handling; do not pass through arbitrary service objects.
- `includes/REST/SettingsController.php`: expose only the safe account summary/activity payload through the existing admin account endpoint or a separately capability-gated read route.
- `src/settings-page/superdav-account-manager.js`: render accessible account activity, credit source, expiry, and usage information with empty and unavailable states.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/SettingsControllerTest.php`: verify response allowlisting, ordering, permission gates, and secret redaction.
- `src/settings-page/__tests__/superdav-account-manager.test.js`: verify formatted activity/expiry states, unknown values, and no-data rendering.

## Required service contract

Confirm a bounded account response that provides only display-safe fields: event type, signed amount in USD micros, effective timestamp, optional expiry timestamp, and a short non-sensitive label/reference. Define the maximum event count and pagination/cursor behaviour. Do not expose invoice IDs, customer identifiers, payment-method metadata, service tokens, raw processor events, or arbitrary descriptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- The page distinguishes purchased, promotional, redeemed, consumed, pending, and expired credits when the service supplies those event types.
- Promotional credit expiry is shown in the site timezone when supplied; absent expiry is labelled as unavailable rather than inferred.
- Activity is newest-first, bounded, and renders an explicit empty state.
- Wallet totals remain server-authoritative; the UI does not recompute a balance from ledger rows.
- Invalid event values or unknown event types are omitted or rendered as a neutral safe state, never as misleading monetary data.
- Responses, browser output, and logs remain free of payment data, tokens, and customer identifiers.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter=SettingsControllerTest
npm run test:js -- superdav-account-manager.test.js
npm run lint
composer phpstan
npm run build
```

Manually test a safe fixture containing purchase, coupon, usage, expiry, and unknown events. Confirm the activity list never changes the displayed authoritative balance and that an account response with secret-like fields does not expose them.

title: consolidated: securely redeem Superdav AI credit coupons
body:
_Supersedes #2332 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Add a secure coupon-redemption flow to the Superdav AI account settings page. An administrator submits a coupon code to the managed Superdav AI service through WordPress, receives only the service's sanitized and refreshed wallet summary, and immediately sees the updated balance and fresh timestamp.

The flow must consume the authoritative service contract delivered by [superdav-ai-service#69](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-service/issues/69) and [superdav-ai-service#71](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-service/pull/71). Use only its defined signed endpoint, request schema, atomic/idempotent outcome, stable error codes, and sanitized wallet response; do not guess an endpoint path or map undocumented errors.

## Why

The current account endpoint reads and refreshes account status but cannot redeem coupons. Administrators need an explicit, safe way to exchange Superdav AI coupon codes for credits without exposing or retaining sensitive entitlement data. The managed service, not the plugin, must make redemption atomic and authoritative.

## How

- In `includes/Core/SuperdavSiteConnectionService.php:111-166`, add a narrowly scoped redemption method beside `refresh_account_status()`. Follow the status refresh's server-to-server bearer-header pattern and its sanitized metadata path. Resolve the redemption endpoint from the documented service contract beside the current endpoint resolver at `:324-339`; send the coupon only in the request body and the stored site bearer token only in request headers. Return the service's sanitized refreshed wallet summary. Do not implement local coupon validation, persistence, retry state, or raw-response logging.
- In `includes/REST/SettingsController.php:132-148`, register a dedicated `manage_options`-gated redemption route beside `/superdav-account`, with a required JSON `coupon_code` argument and validation. Its callback should call the new service method and return only sanitized account status. Preserve the existing account read and manual-refresh behavior, WordPress REST nonce enforcement, and real current-user context. Keep the plugin's private `sd-ai-agent/v1` namespace blocked from agent-facing `wp-rest/execute` dispatch.
- In `src/settings-page/superdav-account-manager.js:80-114` and the account action UI beginning at `:218`, add an accessible coupon input, submit control, pending state, and success/error notices. Submit through the new route; disable submission while active; clear the input after every response; update displayed wallet data from the safe response. Render only stable, actionable error messages and never render coupon, bearer token, or raw upstream payload.
- Extend `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/SettingsControllerTest.php:251-347`, following its server request and token-secrecy assertions, to cover permissions, malformed/missing input, success with refreshed wallet output, stable invalid/expired/already-redeemed responses, upstream failure, no token/coupon/raw-payload disclosure, and preserved administrator restriction.
- Extend `src/settings-page/__tests__/superdav-account-manager.test.js`, following the account-loading fixtures at `:99-123`, to cover validation, submit pending state, input clearing after success and failure, success balance update, and safe error rendering.
- Verify against a disposable service test coupon through the account page and a fresh account-status request without printing a coupon or credential in terminal, tests, logs, notices, or PR output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An administrator with a valid WordPress REST nonce and `manage_options` can redeem a valid coupon from the account page and immediately sees the authoritative refreshed wallet balance with a fresh timestamp.
- [ ] The plugin uses only the endpoint, schema, idempotency behavior, and stable error codes documented by the managed service; it does not guess paths, implement local coupon validation, or translate undocumented errors.
- [ ] Invalid, expired, already-redeemed, and unavailable-service outcomes are actionable without revealing a coupon, bearer token, raw upstream payload, or other sensitive data.
- [ ] The coupon and bearer token are sent only server-to-server (coupon in request body; token in request header), never in query strings, options, transients, REST responses, audit logs, PHP errors, browser analytics, debug notices, or persisted redemption records.
- [ ] The coupon field clears after both successful and failed submissions, and the submit control is disabled while a request is active; retry/duplicate handling remains the upstream idempotency concern.
- [ ] Non-administrative REST requests are rejected, real current-user context is retained, and the agent-facing `wp-rest/execute` ability cannot invoke the private redemption route.
- [ ] Existing balance auto-refresh and manual refresh continue to work after redemption.
- [ ] PHP coverage includes permission, validation, service outcomes, secrecy, and refreshed wallet output; JS coverage includes validation, submit state, field clearing, balance update, and safe errors.
- [ ] `npm run test:php -- --filter=SettingsControllerTest`, `npm run test:js -- superdav-account-manager.test.js`, `npm run lint`, `composer phpstan`, and `npm run build` pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Original scope: the account endpoint currently reads status only; add an explicit server-to-server redemption action that refreshes and displays authoritative wallet data without retaining coupon values.
- Per @superdav42 in the original parent body: redemption requires `manage_options`, a valid REST nonce, the real current-user context, no local coupon persistence/logging/validation, and no agent dispatch through `wp-rest/execute`.
- Per @superdav42 in comment 1: implementation was blocked until the managed service defined a signed endpoint, atomic/idempotent behavior, stable error codes, and a sanitized refreshed-wallet response.
- Per @superdav42 in comment 2: that prerequisite is resolved by service issue #69 and merged PR #71. The client work is unblocked; consume only the service-defined contract and continue to avoid coupon validation, persistence, and logging.
- Rejected/superseded approach: do not infer an endpoint, invent error mappings, or make client-side coupon validation or retry semantics authoritative.

title: consolidated: dedicated account billing actions
body:
_Supersedes #2333 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Add service-issued, action-specific external URLs for **Add credits** and **Manage payment methods** to the Superdav AI account page. Keep **Open account portal** as a separate generic action when its safe service-issued URL is available.

WordPress must render only sanitized metadata returned by the managed account service. It must not derive checkout paths, append query parameters, collect, proxy, store, log, or return card data, bank data, coupon data, billing addresses, or payment responses.

## Why

The account page currently exposes three billing actions through one generic portal URL, so a selected action cannot reliably take the user to the corresponding external billing flow. Distinct account-scoped URLs let users begin the requested external action while preserving the billing service as the sole payment-data boundary.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `includes/Core/SuperdavSiteConnectionService.php:57-72,501-524,556+` — extend `sanitize_remote_metadata()` and `get_status()` to accept `purchase_credits_url` and `payment_methods_url` only when they pass the same HTTPS scheme/host validation and credential-like query-key rejection as `account_portal_url`.
- `includes/REST/SettingsController.php:135-145,526-535` — retain the existing `GET|POST /sd-ai-agent/v1/superdav-account` `manage_options` gate and expose only the sanitized account action metadata.
- `src/settings-page/superdav-account-manager.js:129+` — replace shared generic links with dedicated buttons backed only by service-issued action URLs; use one accurately labelled generic-portal fallback only when a dedicated URL is absent, with no dead or misleading buttons.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/SettingsControllerTest.php:275-402` — cover safe dedicated metadata and omission of URLs containing access tokens, API keys, or other credential-like query keys.
- `src/settings-page/__tests__/superdav-account-manager.test.js` — cover dedicated URL rendering and generic-portal fallback rendering.

### Implementation constraints

1. Confirm the managed-account response supplies non-secret HTTPS `purchase_credits_url` and `payment_methods_url`; the service contract is available from Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-service#68, delivered by merged PR #73.
2. Never fabricate a path from `account_portal_url`, append query parameters, or infer either dedicated action URL.
3. Apply the existing `account_portal_url` allowlist and secret-query-key protection consistently to every remote action URL before persistence and before REST output. Omit unsafe URLs rather than returning them.
4. Keep all payment details in the external Superdav AI billing service. Do not add a WordPress payment form, card field, coupon field, billing-address field, or payment-response handling.
5. Preserve the existing admin-only permission callback on both account routes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Add credits** renders only when the service provides a sanitized purchase URL.
- [ ] **Manage payment methods** renders only when the service provides a sanitized payment-method URL.

- [ ] Missing dedicated URLs render an accurate generic-portal fallback without dead buttons or misleading labels.
- [ ] All three remote URLs use equivalent scheme/host validation and secret-query-key rejection; URLs containing tokens, API keys, access tokens, or similar credential-like keys are omitted from persisted metadata and REST responses.
- [ ] No payment or billing data is collected, proxied, stored, logged, or returned by WordPress.
- [ ] `GET|POST /sd-ai-agent/v1/superdav-account` remains restricted by `manage_options`.
- [ ] Verification passes:

  ```bash

  npm run lint
  composer phpstan
  npm run build
  ```

- [ ] Manual checks use distinct safe action URLs, then each missing or containing a blocked query key; the browser opens only the expected external URL and REST output contains no service tokens.

## Context & Decisions

- The original #2333 body established the problem, the required metadata and UI surfaces, safety constraints, acceptance criteria, and verification plan.
- Per @superdav42 in Comment 1: client work had to wait for dedicated, safe, account-scoped purchase-credit and payment-method URLs from the billing service; the plugin must never derive checkout URLs or accept payment data.
- Per @superdav42 in Comment 2: the prerequisite is resolved by Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-service#68 and merged PR #73. The client work is unblocked. The final agreed approach is to render only the service-issued dedicated URLs, retain the generic-portal fallback, and preserve the external-service payment boundary.

# Expose actionable active-job failure diagnostics without retaining prompts

## Evidence

A production job reached `before_provider_call`, was resumed twice, and later became `abandoned` without a terminal reason. Existing active-job status and `AgentEventLog` provide useful primitives, but operators cannot distinguish local payload rejection, loopback worker termination, provider timeout, or unchanged-checkpoint exhaustion from the chat UI or a safe support export.

## Goal

Make active-job failures actionable and supportable with structured, scrubbed diagnostics that explain what failed, where it failed, and whether the job can safely resume.

## Files and patterns

- `includes/Models/ActiveJobRepository.php` and `includes/Models/DTO/ActiveJobRow.php` — status/error lifecycle.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:1216-1545` — job-status response and safe error sanitization.
- `includes/Core/AgentEventLog.php` and `includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php` — existing allowlisted telemetry patterns.
- `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js` and chat error/action-card components — job-state display.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/SessionControllerTest.php`, `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AgentEventLogTest.php`, and focused JS tests.

## Requirements

1. Record normalized terminal reason, last safe phase, resume count, provider/model, safe request-size class, and compact recovery metadata where available.
2. Distinguish local payload guard, upstream payload rejection, provider timeout, loopback/worker termination, approval wait/expiry, and no-progress resume exhaustion.
3. Provide a safe job-status DTO/UI card with a specific next action: retry, compact, approve/review, start a continuation, or contact support with a correlation ID.
4. Keep raw prompts, tool arguments/results, authorization headers, option values, and stack traces out of database columns, REST responses, and logs.
5. Retain detailed diagnostics only for a bounded period and preserve existing client compatibility.

## Acceptance criteria

- An abandoned job has a structured, sanitized reason rather than an empty status.
- UI and REST distinguish retryable from non-retryable failures and offer the correct recovery action.
- Support telemetry correlates a job with its provider request only through safe IDs/metrics.
- Diagnostic retention is bounded and secret-redaction tests pass.

## Verification

# Execute long-running site changes as durable phased plans

## Evidence

Complex production requests combine discovery, many changes, policy decisions, and verification in one chat turn. A large session can accumulate tens of thousands of messages and fail before the next provider call. The current agent loop is turn/tool oriented; it has no durable plan boundary that lets a long operation continue with a small, purpose-built context.

## Goal

Introduce an opt-in durable plan runner for multi-phase site operations. It must convert a complex request into reviewable phases, keep structured progress outside chat history, and require explicit approval at consequential write boundaries.

## Files and patterns

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — use the existing loop only for bounded planning/execution turns, not as unbounded plan storage.
- `includes/Models/ActiveJobRepository.php` and `includes/Core/Database.php` — follow the durable active-job schema/migration pattern for plans and steps.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php` — expose plan status, approval, cancellation, and continuation under existing session permissions.
- `includes/Automations/HumanApprovalGate.php` — reuse the established approval model rather than inventing a bypass.
- `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js`, `src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js`, and chat action-card components — render phase progress and explicit approval/retry actions.

## Requirements

1. Define a compact plan/step model: scope, preconditions, read/write classification, idempotency key, expected evidence, rollback guidance, and status.
2. Persist completed step summaries and safe outputs independently of raw model transcript/tool payloads.
3. Limit each provider call to the active phase plus a compact plan summary and bounded prior-step evidence.
4. Require explicit confirmation before the first destructive/consequential phase and when scope changes. Never auto-approve tools merely because a plan exists.
5. Resume only idempotent, safe phases after an interruption; present actionable failure state otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

- A multi-phase request can complete after page navigation or an interrupted worker without resending its full conversation history.
- Provider context remains bounded as plan length grows.
- The UI shows current phase, completed evidence, pending confirmation, and safe next action.
- Scope/approval checks survive resume and cannot be overridden by browser-supplied plan state.
- Raw prompts, credentials, and raw tool results are not copied into plan records.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='AgentLoopTest|SessionControllerTest|ActiveJobsCleanupTest|HumanApprovalGateTest'
```

Add an end-to-end fixture with at least four phases, an approval pause, a simulated worker interruption, and bounded request-history assertions.

title: fix: preflight full AI request envelopes and compact oversize chats
body:
# Preflight the full AI request envelope and auto-compact oversize chats

## Evidence

A production multisite chat session accumulated 18,759 persisted messages (about 39.5 MB). Its most recent background job was abandoned after two automatic resumes at `before_provider_call`. The durable checkpoint was about 328 KB while the configured request budget was 512 KB. The current budget calculation applies to history, but the final provider request also includes system instructions, tool definitions, attachments, and model options.

The existing payload work from #2241/#2242 correctly handles history trimming, one reduced 413 retry, and server-backed manual compaction. It does not establish a complete-envelope preflight or automatically offer/create a safe continuation before dispatch.

## Goal

Prevent a large session from repeatedly dispatching an AI request that cannot fit its complete provider envelope. Preserve the source session and create a bounded continuation only when it is safe and useful.

## Files and patterns

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:1569-1669` — existing history-only payload recovery; extend its preflight without adding unbounded retries.
- `includes/Core/ConversationTrimmer.php:136-188` — bounded history trimming; preserve valid tool-call/result cycles.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:905-995` — deterministic server-side continuation-session creation.
- `includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php:407-444` — scrubbed request-size diagnostics.
- `src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js` and the chat session UI — surface an explicit compact-and-continue action; do not silently replace a conversation.

## Requirements

1. Estimate the complete outbound request envelope immediately before dispatch: serialized history, system instruction, tool declarations, attachments, and provider/model options.
2. Enforce a configurable safety margin below the runtime provider limit. Do not expose prompt content, headers, credentials, or raw tool arguments in errors or telemetry.
3. When the envelope cannot fit, skip the provider call and return structured recovery metadata that lets the UI offer a server-side compact continuation.
4. Retain the original session unchanged; the continuation must contain bounded, deterministic context and record `compacted_from`.
5. Preserve the existing one-reduced-payload retry only for a real upstream 413, and only when the reduced complete envelope is materially smaller.

## Acceptance criteria

- An oversized envelope is rejected locally before a provider call, with a safe compact-and-continue affordance.
- The preflight accounts for non-history request components.
- The continuation remains below byte/token budgets, contains no raw attachment/tool payloads, and does not modify the source session.
- Existing 413 recovery behavior remains bounded and provider-neutral.
- Telemetry includes only provider/model, safe size metrics, local/upstream attribution, and recovery outcome.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='AgentLoopTest|ConversationTrimmerTest|SessionControllerTest|ProviderTraceLoggerResolveTest'
npm run test:js -- --runInBand src/store/__tests__/index.test.js
npm run lint:php
npm run lint:js
npm run verify
```

title: fix: prevent no-progress checkpoint resume retries
body:
# Stop retrying unchanged oversized checkpoints and persist compact resume state

## Evidence

A production background job stopped at `before_provider_call` and was automatically resumed twice with no recorded terminal reason. The checkpoint contained a large serialized state. Existing checkpoint recovery in #2026/#2049 and #2316 safely resumes selected phases, but it can retry the same ineffective state until the retry budget is exhausted.

## Goal

Make automatic job recovery progress-aware: resume only when state has changed or a bounded recovery transformation has reduced the next request. Persist compact, inspectable resume state instead of repeatedly serializing the full in-memory transcript and activity log.

## Files and patterns

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:955-978` — current checkpoint payload construction.
- `includes/Models/ActiveJobRepository.php:203-251` — checkpoint persistence and resume-attempt claim.
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:1454-1530` — automatic resume dispatch and safe phases.
- `includes/Models/DTO/ActiveJobRow.php` and `includes/Core/Database.php:715-735` — schema/DTO only if new bounded metadata is necessary.
- `includes/Core/JobErrorSanitizer.php` and `includes/Core/AgentEventLog.php` — client-safe reason codes and scrubbed events.

## Requirements

1. Store a stable, secret-free fingerprint of the next provider input plus byte/token estimates and the checkpoint phase.
2. Before automatic resume, compare the candidate fingerprint and size metadata with the prior attempt. Do not replay an unchanged oversized or locally rejected request.
3. When recovery can compact state, persist the compacted resume history and mark the recovery transformation; otherwise end the job with a structured, actionable terminal reason.
4. Bound checkpoint storage: avoid duplicating unbounded message/tool logs when the session row already owns durable history. Preserve exact tool-execution safety rules; never replay a potentially destructive tool.
5. Migrate existing rows safely and tolerate mixed plugin versions/empty checkpoint metadata.

## Acceptance criteria

- Repeated resumes of identical pre-provider state stop after the first non-progressing attempt with a safe terminal reason.
- A compacted recovery produces a different fingerprint and can resume once.
- Checkpoint storage remains bounded for very large sessions.
- Crash recovery semantics after tool execution are unchanged: no destructive tool replay.
- REST clients receive only sanitized phase/reason/size-class metadata.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='AgentLoopTest|ActiveJobsCleanupTest|RestControllerTest|SessionControllerTest'
```

Add tests for identical retry suppression, compacted-fingerprint resume, mixed-schema rows, and tool-execution checkpoints.

## Evidence

The agent’s generic `run-php` tool is too broad for a complex multisite commerce setup. It cannot communicate a constrained, auditable set of intended changes as clearly as typed abilities, and confirmation currently occurs after the model has generated opaque arbitrary PHP.

## Goal

Provide typed, site-scoped commerce setup abilities that can inspect and prepare a reviewed change plan without allowing a model to escape the requested site scope. The first target is marketplace category/configuration work; unsupported vendor-plugin features must be reported as prerequisites, not improvised with arbitrary PHP.

## Files and patterns

- `includes/Abilities/WooCommerceAbilities.php` — existing WooCommerce ability conventions and validation.
- `includes/Abilities/SiteHealthAbilities.php` — safe multisite inspection patterns.
- `includes/Core/AbilityFunctionResolver.php` and ability schemas — typed input validation and permissions.
- `includes/Automations/HumanApprovalGate.php` — reviewed approval semantics.
- `includes/Core/ChangeLogger.php` — record changed resources without logging sensitive option values.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/*WooCommerce*Test.php` and multisite REST/ability fixtures.

## Requirements

1. Add read-only abilities to inspect the current blog, active commerce/vendor-plugin capabilities, product categories, and supported setting keys.
2. Add a plan ability that accepts an explicit target blog ID and emits a validated, site-scoped proposed change set. Refuse network-wide scope unless a separate explicit network capability is used.
3. Add narrowly scoped execution abilities only for verified supported operations, with the target blog switched/restored safely and an approval gate covering the full reviewed plan.
4. Treat vendor-plugin-only features as capability checks. Return an explicit prerequisite when the active edition/module does not support a requested setting.
5. Do not implement a generic arbitrary-PHP fallback, expose option secrets, or silently apply a setting to subsites.

## Acceptance criteria

- A commerce plan is tied to one requested site and rejects cross-site writes.
- Unsupported vendor-plugin settings return a clear prerequisite rather than fabricated success.
- Approved category/settings operations affect only the target blog and leave a verifiable change log.
- The agent can execute a reviewed plan without `run-php`.
- Tests prove `switch_to_blog()` restoration and zero writes to non-target sites.

Reviewing merged PR #2360 found that `WooCommerceAbilities::execute_approved_plan()` checks `is_woocommerce_runtime_available()` after `switch_to_blog()`. That runtime check uses globally loaded WooCommerce classes/taxonomy, while switching blogs does not load plugins per site.

2. Continue allowing a network-active WooCommerce installation when that is valid for the target site.
3. Fail safely with an actionable prerequisite-changed error before any taxonomy or option write.

# Prevent generated coverage assets from reaching stylelint hooks

## Problem

While preparing PR #2367, the first commit workflow failed because generated, ignored `coverage-html/_css` assets were selected by the CSS lint-staged rule. The source change itself was clean, but the hook attempted to lint generated coverage CSS.

## Target surfaces

- `package.json` lint-staged configuration
- `.husky/pre-commit` and any hook wrapper that expands CSS candidates
- `.gitignore` coverage artifact patterns

## Required behavior

- Pre-commit must lint staged, repository-owned CSS without accepting ignored coverage-report artifacts.
- A generated `coverage-html/` report must not block a valid source commit.
- Do not weaken CSS linting for tracked source or build CSS files.

## Suggested approach

Inspect how lint-staged receives candidate paths and constrain the CSS rule to staged tracked files, or explicitly exclude the ignored coverage-report path. Prefer a deterministic hook/configuration fix over manual deletion of generated reports.

## Verification

1. Run `npm run test:php -- --filter=ActiveJobsCleanupTest` to regenerate coverage artifacts.
2. Run the applicable lint-staged/pre-commit verification with a staged tracked CSS fixture or existing staged CSS change; it must not select `coverage-html/_css`.
3. Run `npm run lint:css`.
4. Confirm `git status --short` contains no generated coverage artifacts and the hook succeeds for the staged tracked file.

title: Fix Plugin Builder isolated-test database credential drift
body:
## Problem

The full PHPUnit suite has three reproducible failures in Plugin Builder sandbox tests because the Layer 2 isolated WordPress subprocess cannot authenticate to the test database, even though the parent PHPUnit process can.

Reproduced on a clean `origin/main` worktree, independent of feature changes:

```text
PluginBuilderIntegrationTest::test_updater_happy_path_replaces_files
PluginUpdaterTest::test_test_staged_passes_for_valid_plugin
PluginUpdaterTest::test_update_replaces_live_plugin_files

mysqli_real_connect(): (HY000/1045): Access denied for user 'root'@'localhost'
Tests: 3, Assertions: 5, Failures: 3
```

Running `npm run test:php:setup` also fails at the `mysqladmin` database-create step with the same authentication error. The setup script writes the WP-CLI-compatible config before that failure, but the isolated subprocess still cannot connect.

## Investigation targets

- `bin/setup-wp-phpunit.php`: reconcile credentials used by the parent test bootstrap, `mysqladmin`, and generated core `wp-config.php` without logging secrets.
- `bin/run-wp-phpunit.php`: verify which test configuration and environment variables reach the parent process.
- `advanced-plugin/includes/PluginBuilder/PluginSandbox.php`: ensure Layer 2 receives the same safe test database configuration as the parent process.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/PluginBuilder/PluginBuilderIntegrationTest.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/PluginBuilder/PluginUpdaterTest.php`

## Expected behaviour

The parent PHPUnit process, setup command, and Layer 2 subprocess should use one consistent test database configuration. Clean local verification must not require exposing or hardcoding credentials.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php:setup
npm run test:php -- --filter='PluginBuilderIntegrationTest::test_updater_happy_path_replaces_files|PluginUpdaterTest::test_test_staged_passes_for_valid_plugin|PluginUpdaterTest::test_update_replaces_live_plugin_files'

All commands should complete with zero failures.

## Summary

The floating widget's slash-command menu renders above the visible viewport on a mobile-width admin screen, making every command visually inaccessible even though the options remain in the accessibility tree.

## Reproduction evidence

Tested from the authenticated floating widget on current `main` at `9fa24d46` with a `390 × 844` viewport:

1. Open the floating widget.
2. Focus the message input at the bottom of the panel.
3. Type `/`.
4. The menu is not visible in the viewport.

Measured DOM rectangles:

```text
panel:   y=72, height=764, bottom=836
listbox: y=-174, height=242, bottom=68
```

The `Slash commands` listbox reports `display: block` and `visibility: visible`, but its entire rectangle is above the viewport. The accessibility snapshot still exposes `/new`, `/model`, `/remember`, `/forget`, `/clear`, `/export`, `/compact`, `/plan`, `/help`, and `/report-issue`.

## Likely cause and target files

- `src/components/chat-widget/widget-input.js`: renders `SlashCommandMenu` inside `.sdaa-w-input` at the bottom of the panel.
- `src/components/slash-command-menu.js`: applies an inline `bottom` position when available.
- `src/admin-page/style.css`: `.sdaa-slash-menu` uses absolute positioning with `bottom: 100%` and a 240px maximum height.
- `src/components/chat-widget/widget.css`: `.sdaa-w-panel` uses `overflow: hidden`; the widget input sits at the bottom of a viewport-height panel.

The popup positioning is not clamped or flipped against the viewport/panel bounds on narrow screens.

## Expected behavior

- The menu should remain keyboard navigable and scroll internally when all commands do not fit.

title: Preserve per-turn model labels in floating-widget history
body:
## Summary

Every historical user message in the floating widget is labelled with the **currently selected** model rather than the model used for that turn. Switching the model retroactively relabels old prompts, which makes the conversation audit trail inaccurate.

## Reproduction evidence

Tested from the authenticated floating widget on current `main` at `9fa24d46`:

1. Select `Superdav Chat Fast` and send several prompts.
2. Confirm each user-message meta row says `Superdav Chat Fast`.
3. Change the selector to `Superdav Chat Pro` without resending anything.
4. Every historical user-message meta row immediately changes to `Superdav Chat Pro`.
5. Change back to Fast; every row changes back to Fast.

The underlying historical responses and session remain unchanged. Only the labels are rewritten by current selector state.

## Likely cause and target files

- `src/components/chat-redesign/message-items.js`: `UserMessage` derives `selectedModelName` from `getSelectedProviderId()` / `getSelectedModelId()` and uses it whenever `messageToken?.modelName` is absent.
- `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js`: per-message metadata is attached to the last **model** message index, so a user-message index generally has no `messageToken` and falls back to the live selector.
- Session REST serialization/hydration and token metadata should be inspected to determine whether the model used for each turn is persisted and mapped to the corresponding user/assistant pair.

## Expected behavior

- Historical message labels should identify the model used for that exchange.
- Changing the active model should affect future sends only.
- If historical model metadata is unavailable, omit the label or show an explicit unknown state rather than displaying the current selector as historical fact.

## Acceptance criteria

- Persist or correctly associate provider/model metadata with each completed exchange.
- `UserMessage` no longer falls back to the current selected model for historical rows.
- Switching models leaves all existing row labels unchanged.
- Newly sent turns show the newly selected model.
- Session reload/hydration preserves the same per-turn labels.
- Add unit coverage around mixed-model conversations and an E2E check that switches models after at least one completed response.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:js -- --runInBand
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- tests/e2e/floating-widget.spec.js tests/e2e/chat-interactions.spec.js
npm run lint:js
npm run build
```

Manual check: send one turn with Fast and one with Pro, reload the page, and verify each turn retains its original model label after further selector changes.

title: Floating widget new-chat actions immediately reopen the latest session
body:
## Summary

The floating widget's **Start new chat** button and `/new` slash command do not start an empty conversation. They briefly clear the current session, then immediately rehydrate the newest existing session. The previous messages remain visible and the selected model resets to the default.

This prevents users from separating unrelated tasks and can accidentally carry prior context into a new request.

## Reproduction evidence

Tested from the authenticated floating widget on current `main` at `9fa24d46` with WordPress 7.0.2:

1. Open an existing widget conversation containing 8 or more message rows.
2. Click the header button labelled `Start new chat`.
3. Observe that the same session title and all prior message rows remain.
4. Type `/new`, select the command, and press Enter.
5. Observe the same result again.

Instrumented result:

- Before: 8 message rows.
- After **Start new chat**: 8 message rows, same session title.
- After `/new`: 10 message rows, same session title.
- The selected model also changed from `Superdav Chat Fast` back to the default `Superdav Chat Pro`.

## Likely cause and target files

- `src/components/chat-widget/widget-header.js`: `handleNewChat()` calls `clearCurrentSession()`.
- `src/components/chat-widget/widget-input.js`: `/new` and `/clear` call the same action.
- `src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js`: `clearCurrentSession()` dispatches `CLEAR_CURRENT_SESSION` but does not record that the clear was an explicit user action.
- `src/floating-widget/index.js`: once `currentSessionId` becomes empty, the hydration effect calls `getHydrationSessionId()` and reopens the newest session.
- `src/floating-widget/frontend-onboarding.js`: `getHydrationSessionId()` correctly restores sessions on initial load, but needs an explicit-new-chat opt-out so the fix from #2087 does not override user intent.

## Expected behavior

- Header **Start new chat**, `/new`, and `/clear` should immediately show the empty state with zero prior messages.
- The next sent prompt should create a distinct session.
- Initial page load/navigation should continue restoring active/latest sessions as implemented for #2087.
- Starting a new chat should not unexpectedly change the currently selected model unless that behavior is explicitly designed and communicated.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a store-level or component-level explicit-new-chat guard that prevents the hydration effect from reopening an old session after user-initiated clearing.
- Preserve active/latest session hydration on genuine page load and navigation.
- Add regression coverage for both the header button and `/new` in the floating widget.
- Assert the message list becomes empty and remains empty until the user sends another prompt.
- Assert the next prompt creates/opens a different session ID.
- Decide and test whether model selection is preserved; avoid silent fallback.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:js -- --runInBand
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- tests/e2e/floating-widget.spec.js tests/e2e/chat-interactions.spec.js
npm run lint:js
npm run build
```

title: Stock image failure leaves generated photography site without photos
body:
## Description
A thumbs-down report says the agent built a photography/PTO-style site but did not add any photos. The session shows the agent called `sd-ai-agent/stock-image`, which returned `success: true` while also returning an empty `url`, `attachment_id: 0`, and an error that all free image sources failed because Openverse returned HTTP 403. The agent then created five pages using text-only markdown content and did not recover by calling `sd-ai-agent/generate-image` or otherwise adding visual media.

## Expected Behavior
When stock-image retrieval fails, the agent should treat the missing image URL as a failed image acquisition, recover with an available image-generation/media workflow, or clearly explain that photos could not be added instead of publishing a photography site with no images.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a fresh WordPress site using the Ollie block theme, ask the agent: `I would like help setting up my website from scratch.`
2. Continue with a photography website / photo shoot booking setup.
3. Observe the tool sequence:

4. Review the generated site. No photos or image blocks were added even though the site type depends on visual examples.

## Worker Guidance
- Inspect `includes/Abilities/StockImageAbility.php` and any caller/result-normalization code for the stock image ability. A result with an empty URL and an error should not be indistinguishable from a successful image acquisition.

title: feedback: scope tool calls to targeted message context
body:
## Description
Targeted thumbs-down feedback reports scope `session_data.messages` to the selected message context but include the entire session-wide `tool_calls` log. This produces internally inconsistent and unnecessarily large reports that can mislead triage.

Reports 51 and 52 were submitted from the same session. Report 52 contains four scoped messages for a plugin-review prompt and its first two tool calls, while its payload contains 866 historical tool-log entries (433 calls and 433 responses), including unrelated file, database, REST, and cleanup operations. Report 51 shows the same pattern with 862 entries.

## Expected Behavior
When `message_index` requests a targeted message window, the feedback payload should include only tool calls and responses associated with that window, or explicitly omit the tool log when it cannot be mapped safely. `message_count`, `tool_call_count`, messages, and tool calls should describe the same feedback context.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use one chat session for a long tool-heavy task.
2. Continue the same session with a distinct prompt.
3. Submit thumbs-down feedback for a message in the later prompt.
4. Inspect the generated payload.
5. Observe that `ReportBuilder::slice_message_context()` scopes messages, but `session_data.tool_calls` still contains the complete session log.

- Add focused coverage in a feedback report-builder test for a session containing tool calls before, within, and after the selected message window.
- Ensure `build_summary()` reports the same scoped tool-call count as `build()`.

title: Require clarification before public mutations from underspecified prompts
body:
## Summary

A vague, low-information request can trigger an arbitrary public site mutation instead of a clarification or a bounded, reversible inspection. In the reproduced session, the first user message was `do anything`; the General agent immediately loaded the content skill and published a new blog post with invented subject matter.

Publishing arbitrary content is not a safe interpretation of an underspecified prompt, even when the current user has permission to publish.

## Reproduction evidence

Local session 16 (`wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions`) recorded this sequence:

1. User: `do anything`
2. Model: loads `content-management`
3. Model: calls `sd-ai-agent/create-post` with `status: publish`
4. Post 66 is published as “How to Feel Effortless in Your Wedding Photos”

No site inspection, candidate-plan summary, clarification, draft staging, or approval boundary occurred before publication.

## Expected behavior

When intent, target, and success criteria are all absent, the agent should not invent a public mutation. It should do one of the following:

- ask a concise clarifying question;
- offer a small set of explicit candidate actions;
- perform only readonly inspection and report a recommendation; or
- if a harmless demonstration is intentionally supported, stage it as a draft and clearly identify it as a proposal.

Explicit user requests such as “publish a post about X” must continue to work normally.

## Relevant implementation

Inspect the narrowest deterministic enforcement point rather than relying only on model judgment:

- `includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php`
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php`
- mutating ability annotations and confirmation routing
- `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php`
- General agent defaults in `includes/Models/Agent.php`

## Acceptance criteria

- Define a testable low-information/ambiguous-turn policy for the first mutating action of a turn.
- A bare prompt such as `do anything` cannot directly publish, delete, activate, install, send, or otherwise make a public/external mutation.
- The guard does not block clearly specified mutations.
- The UI receives a clarification/proposal rather than a generic provider error.
- Add regression coverage for a vague prompt followed by a proposed `create-post(status=publish)` call.
- Document which mutation classes require clarification versus which readonly operations remain available.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run test:php -- --filter='AgentLoopTest|SystemInstructionBuilderTest|PostAbilitiesTest'
pnpm run test:js -- --runInBand
```

title: Deduplicate failed-job recovery history across optional message metadata
body:
## Summary

Failed-job recovery can append an entire conversation a second time when semantically identical serialized messages differ only in optional metadata such as `provider_id` and `model_id`.

This duplicates prompts, assistant replies, and historical tool calls in `wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions.messages`, inflating provider context and making later turns ambiguous.

## Reproduction evidence

Session 16 contained:

- messages 0–9: the original `do anything` / post creation / follow-up exchange, including provider/model metadata;
- messages 10–19: the same roles, parts, text, function calls, and function responses repeated without that metadata;
- messages 20–21: `but I don't, check it yourself` persisted twice.

Only one post was created, proving this was history duplication rather than a second intentional execution.

## Likely root cause

`SessionController::append_history_delta_to_session()` calls `get_history_append_offset()`. That method compares complete rows with strict array identity. When existing persisted rows contain optional provider/model fields but recovery serialization omits them, the common-prefix check fails at index 0. The fallback can then treat the full recovery history as a new suffix.

`SessionRepository::append()` subsequently uses `array_merge()` without an idempotency guard.

## Expected behavior

Recovery persistence should append only the genuinely new suffix. Message identity must be based on canonical conversation semantics (role, ordered parts, function-call/result IDs and payload) while ignoring transport-only metadata. Legitimate repeated user messages must not be globally deduplicated.

## Relevant implementation

- `includes/REST/SessionController.php`
  - `persist_error_recovery_to_session()`
  - `append_history_delta_to_session()`
  - `get_history_append_offset()`
- `includes/Repositories/SessionRepository.php::append()`
- `includes/Core/ConversationSerializer.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/RestControllerTest.php`

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a canonical ordered-prefix comparator that ignores only documented non-semantic metadata.
- A full recovery history with provider/model metadata added or removed appends only the failed turn.
- A suffix-only recovery payload still appends correctly.
- Two genuinely repeated user turns remain two turns.
- Replaying the same recovery persistence operation is idempotent.
- Tool call and function response ordering/IDs remain intact.
- Add a regression fixture matching the observed 10-message replay.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run test:php -- --filter='RestControllerTest|DatabaseTest|ConversationSerializerTest'
```

title: Record retry-exhausted provider transport failures in provider traces
body:
## Summary

Provider tracing does not preserve enough information for retry-exhausted transport failures. Successful HTTP/SDK pairs are recorded, but failed network attempts are either absent or reduced to an uninformative SDK row with `error=no_result_event`.

Operators therefore cannot answer which status/transport error occurred, how many attempts ran, whether `Retry-After` was present, or whether failure happened before or after a client-tool continuation.

## Reproduction evidence

Two failures were observed for `sd-ai-agent-cloud / superdav-chat-pro`:

1. At `2026-08-15 05:13:29 UTC`, the event log records `sd_ai_agent_provider_retry_failed` after 4 attempts over 12 seconds. There is no corresponding failed row in `wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace`; adjacent rows are HTTP 200.
2. At `2026-08-15 06:00:39 UTC`, trace 817 is only `source=sdk`, `status_code=0`, `duration_ms=7033`, `error=no_result_event`. No HTTP failure row records the four failed attempts or classified timeout.

The event log has the useful `provider_timeout` classification, but the trace table does not.

## Expected behavior

A traced provider invocation that exhausts retries should produce a bounded, redacted terminal trace record with safe diagnostics: provider/model, classified error code, status when known, attempt count, elapsed time, request-size class, retry-after/backoff metadata, session/job correlation, and phase.

Raw credentials and unredacted prompt data must not be added to failure diagnostics.

## Relevant implementation

- `includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php`
- `includes/Core/AiClientEventTraceLogger.php`
- `includes/Bootstrap/HttpTraceHandler.php`
- `includes/Bootstrap/AiClientEventTraceHandler.php`
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php::send_prompt()` retry path
- `includes/Models/ProviderTrace.php`
- trace and event logger tests

## Acceptance criteria

- Retry exhaustion always produces one terminal provider trace when tracing is enabled.
- Transport `WP_Error`/exception paths retain a safe classified error instead of only `no_result_event`.
- Attempts are correlated as one invocation, or individually linked without misleading duplicate calls.
- Trace output identifies `initial provider call` versus `client_tool_resume`.
- Existing header/body redaction and the debug-only trace gate remain intact.
- Tests cover timeout, DNS/connect failure, 429 with `Retry-After`, and success-after-retry.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run test:php -- --filter='ProviderTrace|AiClientEventTrace|HttpTraceHandler|AgentLoopTest'
```
